1	"""Datasource adapter seam.
2	
3	Every datasource (Snowflake now; ADLS / S3 / Unity Catalog later) executes DQ
4	checks behind one ``CheckRunner`` interface that speaks GX-agnostic DTOs. The
5	GX-specific machinery lives entirely inside each adapter, so the run-service and
6	its tests depend only on the types here — never on Great Expectations internals.
7	This is also the seam that lets v1.1 swap GX for DQX on Unity Catalog (CLAUDE.md
8	§5) without rippling into the suite / check / result layer.
9	
10	`CheckSpec` goes in (a check pulled from the DB); `CheckOutcome` comes out, one
11	per check, shaped to map cleanly onto the `results` table columns. Adapters
12	translate GX results into these DTOs; tests provide a fake `CheckRunner` and
13	never touch a live datasource.
14	"""
15	
16	from __future__ import annotations
17	
18	from dataclasses import dataclass
19	from typing import Any, Protocol, runtime_checkable
20	
21	from pydantic import BaseModel
22	
23	
24	@dataclass(frozen=True)
25	class CheckSpec:
26	    """One expectation to evaluate, sourced from a `checks` row.
27	
28	    `expectation_type` is the GX snake_case name (e.g.
29	    ``expect_column_values_to_not_be_null``); `kwargs` are its parameters
30	    (e.g. ``{"column": "id"}``). Adapters own the translation to the concrete
31	    GX expectation class.
32	    """
33	
34	    expectation_type: str
35	    kwargs: dict[str, Any]
36	
37	
38	@dataclass(frozen=True)
39	class CheckOutcome:
40	    """Result of one check, shaped for the `results` table.
41	
42	    `observed_value` / `expected_value` / `sample_failures` land in the
43	    matching JSONB columns. `sample_failures` may contain real data rows, so it
44	    is governed by the retention sweep and must only ever be logged through the
45	    PII-redacting structlog chain.
46	    """
47	
48	    expectation_type: str
49	    success: bool
50	    observed_value: dict[str, Any] | None = None
51	    expected_value: dict[str, Any] | None = None
52	    sample_failures: dict[str, Any] | None = None
53	
54	
55	@dataclass(frozen=True)
56	class SuiteOutcome:
57	    """Aggregate result of running a list of checks against one table."""
58	
59	    success: bool
60	    checks: list[CheckOutcome]
61	
62	
63	@runtime_checkable
64	class CheckRunner(Protocol):
65	    """Executes a set of checks against a single table and returns outcomes."""
66	
67	    def run_checks(
68	        self,
69	        *,
70	        table: str,
71	        schema: str | None,
72	        checks: list[CheckSpec],
73	    ) -> SuiteOutcome: ...
74	
75	
76	@runtime_checkable
77	class ConnectionAdapter(Protocol):
78	    """Per-datasource-type connection behaviour: config validation + live test.
79	
80	    The two things that vary across connection types (Snowflake now; ADF, ADLS,
81	    S3, Unity Catalog next) behind one interface, so connection-CRUD service code
82	    dispatches by ``connection.type`` and never branches on it. Each adapter owns
83	    its own pydantic config model; both methods take the raw config dict so the
84	    adapter is the single source of truth for that type's shape.
85	
86	    `validate_config` parses + validates a stored/incoming config (raising
87	    pydantic ``ValidationError`` on bad input) and returns the normalised model.
88	    `test` resolves connectivity against the live datasource using the config +
89	    its secret, raising on failure. Adapters never touch the DB or SecretStore —
90	    the caller resolves the secret and hands it in.
91	    """
92	
93	    def validate_config(self, raw: dict[str, Any]) -> BaseModel: ...
94	
95	    def test(self, raw: dict[str, Any], secret: str) -> None: ...
96

1	"""Connection-type → adapter registry.
2	
3	The single place that maps a ``Connection.type`` to its `ConnectionAdapter`.
4	Adding a datasource type (ADF, ADLS Gen2, S3, Unity Catalog — Weeks 2-3) is a
5	one-line entry here plus the adapter itself; connection-CRUD service code stays
6	untouched, dispatching through `get_connection_adapter`.
7	"""
8	
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	from backend.app.datasources.base import ConnectionAdapter
12	from backend.app.datasources.snowflake import SnowflakeConnectionAdapter
13	
14	
15	class UnsupportedConnectionTypeError(ValueError):
16	    """Raised when no adapter is registered for a connection type."""
17	
18	
19	_ADAPTERS: dict[str, ConnectionAdapter] = {
20	    "snowflake": SnowflakeConnectionAdapter(),
21	}
22	
23	
24	def get_connection_adapter(conn_type: str) -> ConnectionAdapter:
25	    adapter = _ADAPTERS.get(conn_type)
26	    if adapter is None:
27	        raise UnsupportedConnectionTypeError(
28	            f"No connection adapter registered for type {conn_type!r}"
29	        )
30	    return adapter

1	"""Connection CRUD + connectivity test, datasource-type-agnostic.
2	
3	Drives the `connections` table and dispatches type-specific behaviour through
4	the `ConnectionAdapter` registry — so this layer never branches on
5	``connection.type``. Credentials are written through the `SecretStore`
6	(`set`) and only ever referenced by `Connection.secret_ref`; the plaintext
7	secret is never stored on the row or logged.
8	
9	FastAPI-free by design (like `run_service`): takes a `Session` + `SecretStore`,
10	returns ORM models, raises `DataQError` subclasses. The API layer owns
11	request/response shapes and dependency wiring.
12	"""
13	
14	from __future__ import annotations
15	
16	import uuid
17	from typing import Any
18	
19	from pydantic import ValidationError
20	from sqlalchemy import select
21	from sqlalchemy.exc import IntegrityError
22	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
23	
24	from backend.app.core.errors import DataQError
25	from backend.app.core.logging import get_logger
26	from backend.app.core.secrets import SecretNotFoundError, SecretStore
27	from backend.app.datasources.registry import (
28	    UnsupportedConnectionTypeError,
29	    get_connection_adapter,
30	)
31	from backend.app.db.models import ENVS, Connection
32	
33	log = get_logger(__name__)
34	
35	
36	class ConnectionNotFoundError(DataQError):
37	    status_code = 404
38	    code = "connection_not_found"
39	
40	
41	class ConnectionConfigInvalidError(DataQError):
42	    status_code = 422
43	    code = "connection_config_invalid"
44	
45	
46	class ConnectionConflictError(DataQError):
47	    status_code = 409
48	    code = "connection_conflict"
49	
50	
51	class ConnectionTestFailedError(DataQError):
52	    status_code = 502
53	    code = "connection_test_failed"
54	
55	
56	def _validated_config(conn_type: str, config: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
57	    """Reject an unknown type or a config that fails its adapter's schema."""
58	    try:
59	        adapter = get_connection_adapter(conn_type)
60	    except UnsupportedConnectionTypeError as exc:
61	        raise ConnectionConfigInvalidError(str(exc), detail={"type": conn_type}) from exc
62	    try:
63	        adapter.validate_config(config)
64	    except ValidationError as exc:
65	        raise ConnectionConfigInvalidError(
66	            f"Invalid config for {conn_type!r} connection",
67	            detail={"errors": exc.errors()},
68	        ) from exc
69	
70	
71	def _validate_env(env: str) -> None:
72	    """Reject an env outside the allowed set before it hits the DB CHECK."""
73	    if env not in ENVS:
74	        raise ConnectionConfigInvalidError(f"invalid env {env!r}", detail={"allowed": list(ENVS)})
75	
76	
77	def create_connection(
78	    session: Session,
79	    *,
80	    name: str,
81	    conn_type: str,
82	    env: str,
83	    config: dict[str, Any],
84	    secret: str | None,
85	    created_by: uuid.UUID,
86	    secret_store: SecretStore,
87	) -> Connection:
88	    """Validate, persist, and (if a secret is given) write its credential.
89	
90	    The secret_ref is derived from the row's own id (``conn-<uuid>``) — unique
91	    and safe as a Key Vault secret name. The credential is written through the
92	    store; only the ref is persisted on the row.
93	    """
94	    _validated_config(conn_type, config)
95	    _validate_env(env)
96	
97	    conn = Connection(
98	        name=name,
99	        type=conn_type,
100	        env=env,
101	        config=config,
102	        secret_ref=None,
103	        created_by=created_by,
104	    )
105	    session.add(conn)
106	    try:
107	        session.flush()  # assign conn.id + surface the (name, env) unique violation
108	        if secret is not None:
109	            secret_ref = f"conn-{conn.id}"
110	            secret_store.set(secret_ref, secret)
111	            conn.secret_ref = secret_ref
112	        session.commit()
113	    except IntegrityError as exc:
114	        session.rollback()
115	        raise ConnectionConflictError(
116	            "a connection with this name already exists in this env",
117	            detail={"name": name, "env": env},
118	        ) from exc
119	
120	    session.refresh(conn)
121	    log.info("connection_created", connection_id=str(conn.id), type=conn_type, env=env)
122	    return conn
123	
124	
125	def list_connections(
126	    session: Session,
127	    *,
128	    conn_type: str | None = None,
129	    env: str | None = None,
130	) -> list[Connection]:
131	    stmt = select(Connection).order_by(Connection.created_at.desc())
132	    if conn_type is not None:
133	        stmt = stmt.where(Connection.type == conn_type)
134	    if env is not None:
135	        stmt = stmt.where(Connection.env == env)
136	    return list(session.scalars(stmt))
137	
138	
139	def get_connection(session: Session, connection_id: uuid.UUID) -> Connection:
140	    conn = session.get(Connection, connection_id)
141	    if conn is None:
142	        raise ConnectionNotFoundError(
143	            "connection not found", detail={"connection_id": str(connection_id)}
144	        )
145	    return conn
146	
147	
148	def update_connection(
149	    session: Session,
150	    connection_id: uuid.UUID,
151	    *,
152	    name: str | None = None,
153	    config: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
154	    secret: str | None = None,
155	    secret_store: SecretStore,
156	) -> Connection:
157	    """Partial update of name / config / secret. Type and env are immutable."""
158	    conn = get_connection(session, connection_id)
159	
160	    if config is not None:
161	        _validated_config(conn.type, config)
162	        conn.config = config
163	    if name is not None:
164	        conn.name = name
165	    if secret is not None:
166	        secret_ref = conn.secret_ref or f"conn-{conn.id}"
167	        secret_store.set(secret_ref, secret)
168	        conn.secret_ref = secret_ref
169	
170	    try:
171	        session.commit()
172	    except IntegrityError as exc:
173	        session.rollback()
174	        raise ConnectionConflictError(
175	            "a connection with this name already exists in this env",
176	            detail={"connection_id": str(connection_id)},
177	        ) from exc
178	    session.refresh(conn)
179	    log.info("connection_updated", connection_id=str(conn.id))
180	    return conn
181	
182	
183	def delete_connection(session: Session, connection_id: uuid.UUID) -> None:
184	    conn = get_connection(session, connection_id)
185	    session.delete(conn)
186	    session.commit()
187	    log.info("connection_deleted", connection_id=str(connection_id))
188	
189	
190	def test_connection(
191	    session: Session,
192	    connection_id: uuid.UUID,
193	    *,
194	    secret_store: SecretStore,
195	) -> None:
196	    """Resolve the connection's secret and probe live connectivity.
197	
198	    Raises `ConnectionTestFailedError` (502) on missing credentials or any
199	    adapter-reported connectivity failure.
200	    """
201	    conn = get_connection(session, connection_id)
202	    adapter = get_connection_adapter(conn.type)
203	
204	    if not conn.secret_ref:
205	        raise ConnectionTestFailedError(
206	            "connection has no stored credential to test with",
207	            detail={"connection_id": str(connection_id)},
208	        )
209	    try:
210	        secret = secret_store.get(conn.secret_ref)
211	    except SecretNotFoundError as exc:
212	        raise ConnectionTestFailedError(
213	            "credential could not be resolved", detail={"connection_id": str(connection_id)}
214	        ) from exc
215	
216	    try:
217	        adapter.test(dict(conn.config), secret)
218	    except Exception as exc:
219	        log.warning(
220	            "connection_test_failed",
221	            connection_id=str(connection_id),
222	            error_type=type(exc).__name__,
223	        )
224	        # Don't echo the adapter exception to the client — it can carry DSN /
225	        # credential fragments (it's also kept out of the logs above). The
226	        # original is preserved as __cause__ for server-side traceback only.
227	        raise ConnectionTestFailedError(
228	            "connection test failed", detail={"connection_id": str(connection_id)}
229	        ) from exc
230	
231	    log.info("connection_test_succeeded", connection_id=str(connection_id))
232

"""Snowflake datasource adapter (GX Core 1.17).

All Great-Expectations-specific machinery for Snowflake lives here, behind the
`CheckRunner` seam in ``base.py`` — per CLAUDE.md, the GX version-specific API
must not leak into the suite / check / result layer (GX v1 has drifted across
point releases).

The full GX chain (``add_snowflake`` → ``add_table_asset`` →
``add_batch_definition_whole_table`` → ``ValidationDefinition.run``) connects to
Snowflake at asset-build time, so ``run_checks`` cannot run without a live
warehouse. Tests therefore exercise the GX-free parts directly — config
validation, connection-string building, the snake_case→GX-class translation,
and the GX-result→`CheckOutcome` mapping (fed a canned result) — and inject a
fake `CheckRunner` elsewhere. End-to-end validation against a real Snowflake DEV
warehouse is a tracked follow-up.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any
from urllib.parse import quote_plus

import great_expectations as gx
import great_expectations.expectations as gxe
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field

from backend.app.core.secrets import SecretStore
from backend.app.datasources.base import CheckOutcome, CheckSpec, SuiteOutcome

# GX result keys that describe failing rows — copied into CheckOutcome.sample_failures.
# These may contain real data, so they only ever reach logs via the redactor.
_SAMPLE_KEYS = ("partial_unexpected_list", "unexpected_count", "unexpected_percent")

# GX injects internal bookkeeping keys into expectation_config.kwargs at run
# time (e.g. batch_id); strip them so expected_value persists only the check's
# own parameters.
_GX_INTERNAL_KWARGS = frozenset({"batch_id"})


class UnknownExpectationError(ValueError):
    """Raised when a check's expectation_type has no matching GX expectation."""


class SnowflakeConfig(BaseModel):
    """Non-secret Snowflake connection config (the password comes from secrets).

    Maps from ``Connection.config``. ``schema`` is aliased to ``schema_`` to
    avoid shadowing pydantic's ``BaseModel.schema``.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(populate_by_name=True, extra="forbid")

    account: str
    user: str
    database: str
    schema_: str = Field(alias="schema")
    warehouse: str
    role: str | None = None

1	# ADR 0011 — Extensibility seams for deferred connectors and integrations
2	
3	- **Status:** Accepted
4	- **Date:** 2026-05-29
5	- **Deciders:** @TheurgicDuke771
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	Three forward-looking expansion questions were raised against the v1 architecture:
10	
11	1. **More datasources** — additional RDBMS (MS-SQL, BigQuery) and non-RDBMS / streaming (Kafka) beyond the four v1 types.
12	2. **Test-management integration** — push DQ results to JIRA / TestRail / Xray after a suite run.
13	3. **dbt** — where it fits in the model.
14	
15	None of these is in v1 scope (v1 is the four named datasources + two orchestration providers). The question is *timing*: take them up now, or after v1 — and how to avoid an expensive retrofit either way. The recurring answer is the same shape as ADR 0010: **build the seam in v1 where v1 work already touches it, defer the second implementation to post-v1.**
16	
17	## Decision
18	
19	**Defer all three builds to after v1. Shape the v1 work that already touches each area as a generic seam, so the later add is a small additive change rather than a retrofit.**
20	
21	### 1. Datasource extensibility — generic runner dispatch (build the seam in v1)
22	
23	- The `CheckRunner` Protocol (`datasources/base.py`) already isolates per-adapter logic. The gap is the worker: `worker/tasks.py` currently hardwires the Snowflake runner.
24	- **v1 action:** the `run_suite` dispatch must select the `CheckRunner` by `connection.type` (generic), not special-case Snowflake. This is required anyway to land the v1 flat-file and Unity Catalog run paths (Week 5).
25	- **Post-v1:** a new RDBMS datasource (MS-SQL, BigQuery, Postgres) is then a new `CheckRunner` implementation + a `CONNECTION_TYPES` enum value — a day or two each, no core changes.
26	- **Out of scope / not this seam:** **streaming (Kafka) is not "just another adapter."** GX is batch-only (ADR 0003); Kafka needs a *second DQ engine*, which is the DQX v1.1 decision (ADR 0003), not a connector add. Tracked there, not here.
27	
28	### 2. Result publishing — `ResultPublisher` seam (build the seam in v1)
29	
30	- v1 already ships an **outbound MS Teams alert** path (Week 6). Rather than hardcode Teams, build it behind a small `ResultPublisher` interface invoked at the run-completion point (after `run_service.execute_run`).
31	- **PII policy baked in from day one:** `results.sample_failures` may contain sensitive rows (it is exactly what the logger redacts — `core/logging.py`). Any publisher that exports results outside DataQ's trust boundary must apply a redaction / opt-in policy. This applies to the v1 Teams publisher too.
32	- **Post-v1:** JIRA / TestRail / Xray become additional `ResultPublisher` subscribers — no re-plumbing. Natural mapping: suite → test run/cycle, check → test case, passed/failed/skipped → test status; `observed_value` / `expected_value` populate the result body.
33	
34	### 3. dbt — an orchestration provider, not a datasource or a second engine
35	
36	- When/if added, dbt slots behind the existing `OrchestrationProvider` abstraction (ADR 0004) as a **third provider**: a `dbt build`/`dbt test` completion event hits `/api/v1/orchestration/events/dbt`, lands in `pipeline_runs`, and fires the matching `trigger_binding`. dbt Cloud has webhooks; dbt Core can POST from an `on-run-end` hook.
37	- dbt is **not** a datasource (do not add it to the connection/check/suite model — same anti-pattern ADR 0004 guards against) and **not** a second DQ engine for v1.
38	- **Timing:** depends on the `OrchestrationProvider` interface + events router, which are Week 2 work and do not exist yet. dbt rides on top once ADF + Airflow have proven the interface — realistically post-v1. No v1 action beyond keeping `OrchestrationProvider` provider-agnostic (already an ADR 0004 rule).
39	
40	## Consequences
41	
42	**Positive**
43	- Each deferred feature becomes a cheap additive change (new `CheckRunner`, new `ResultPublisher`, new `OrchestrationProvider`) instead of a retrofit, because the seam is built during v1 work we are doing regardless.
44	- No v1 scope creep — zero new v1 features, only "build the seam generically rather than as a one-off."
45	- PII handling for result export is settled once, at the seam, not per-integration.
46	
47	**Negative**
48	- Slightly more deliberate design in three v1 touch-points (worker dispatch, Teams notifier, orchestration interface) than the quickest possible hardcoded version. Accepted — the generic form is barely more code and each is touched in v1 anyway.
49	
50	## Alternatives considered
51	
52	- **Ingest dbt's own native test results as DQ results** — rejected for v1. Collides with GX-only (ADR 0003): it introduces a second result shape and second check semantics, the exact thing the single-result-schema decision avoids. Revisit as a generic "external DQ result ingestion" feature later (shares machinery with the result-publishing seam).
53	- **Treat Kafka as just another `CheckRunner` adapter** — rejected. A batch engine cannot do streaming DQ; this is the DQX engine decision (ADR 0003), not a connector.
54	- **Build JIRA/TestRail integration during v1** — rejected. Net-new, on no roadmap, unblocks nothing in v1. Deferred, with only the `ResultPublisher` seam built now.
55	
56	## Related
57	
58	- ADR 0003 — GX-only for v1 (streaming/DQX boundary; single result schema).
59	- ADR 0004 — `OrchestrationProvider` abstraction (dbt as a third provider).
60	- ADR 0010 — provider-agnostic infrastructure seams (the infra-side counterpart).
61	- `datasources/base.py` (`CheckRunner`), `worker/tasks.py` (dispatch), `services/run_service.py` (completion hook point).
62	- v1 action items tracked in `docs/progress.md` (Week 5 generic dispatch, Week 6 `ResultPublisher` seam).
63

1	# Architecture Decision Records (ADRs)
2	
3	Each ADR captures a single significant architecture decision: the context, the decision, the consequences, and the alternatives considered. New ADRs are append-only — supersede an old decision by adding a new ADR and marking the old one's status as `Superseded by ADR-NNNN`.
4	
5	## Format
6	
7	- File name: `NNNN-short-kebab-slug.md` (zero-padded 4-digit sequence)
8	- Frontmatter fields: Status, Date, Deciders
9	- Sections: Context, Decision, Consequences, Alternatives considered, Related (optional)
10	- Keep each ADR short — 1–2 pages. If it grows past that, the decision is probably two decisions.
11	
12	## Index
13

97:### Severity threshold tiers (warn / fail / critical)
98:> **Design decision required upfront:** agree health score weighting before building — e.g. warn = 0.5 penalty, fail = 1.0, critical = 2.0. This affects the DB schema for run results and cannot be changed cheaply after data is written.
99:- [ ] Add optional `warn_threshold`, `fail_threshold`, `critical_threshold` fields to check model — all nullable; if only one threshold set, check behaves as standard pass/fail
100:- [ ] Alembic migration — add threshold columns + `status` enum (`pass`, `warn`, `fail`, `critical`) to `checks` / `check_results`, **plus the monitor-kind + metric columns below (one migration, not three — the schema can't be changed cheaply once results are written)**
101:- [ ] Post-processing logic in GX result handler — after GX returns binary result, evaluate observed value against thresholds to derive `warn` / `fail` / `critical` status
102:- [ ] Update check CRUD API to accept and return threshold fields; update run result response schema to include new status values and health score weighting config
105:> **Design decision required upfront (ADR `0012`, TBD W3):** decide the `check.kind` discriminator + numeric metric storage *before* writing the threshold migration — they ride the **same** migration, so there's no second backward-compatible two-step. v1 implements `expectation` only; the seam keeps freshness / volume / schema-drift / anomaly (v1.x, Theme A below) from forcing a check/result schema rewrite later. It is the one seam orthogonal to the datasource seams (`CheckRunner`, `ConnectionAdapter`) — it varies by *monitor kind*, not by datasource.

107:- [ ] Generalise the run path to dispatch by `check.kind` — `expectation` → the GX `CheckRunner`; other kinds raise `NotImplementedError` until their v1.x impls land
108:- [ ] Add `metric_value` (NUMERIC, nullable) + `duration_ms` (INT, nullable) to results — fold into the threshold migration. `metric_value` is the scalar a monitor measured (SQL-aggregatable — JSONB `observed_value` can't be `AVG()`/`STDDEV()`'d — so Week-6 trends + v1.1 anomaly baselines both reuse it); `duration_ms` is per-check runtime for the cost/perf surface (Theme E)

358:- Volume anomaly detection — `kind=volume`: row-count drift beyond % vs a rolling N-day baseline (dynamic baseline, not a static threshold)
359:- Schema-drift monitor — `kind=schema_drift`: auto-detect column add / remove / type change across runs
360:- Anomaly detection — `kind=anomaly`: learned baselines (mean / stddev / seasonality) on any numeric `metric_value`
364:- Quality gate (write-audit-publish) — synchronous `evaluate → pass/fail` endpoint a pipeline calls to hold publish on a `critical` failure
```

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/docs/adr/0005-severity-tier-weights.md",
  "content": "# ADR 0005 — Severity tier weights (warn / fail / critical → health score)\n\n- **Status:** Accepted\n- **Date:** 2026-05-30\n- **Deciders:** @TheurgicDuke771\n\n## Context\n\nv1 checks are not binary pass/fail. A check can carry up to three optional\nthresholds (`warn_threshold`, `fail_threshold`, `critical_threshold`), and a run\nresult lands in one of four states: `pass`, `warn`, `fail`, `critical`. The\ndashboard (Week 6) rolls these per-result states up into a single **health\nscore** stat card + 7-day trend, and alert routing (Week 6) keys off the same\ntiers (`warn` quiet, `fail` standard, `critical` @channel).\n\nThis decision must land **before the Week-3 threshold migration** because two\nthings bake into schema and stored data:\n\n1. The `status` value set (`pass | warn | fail | critical`) becomes a CHECK\n   constraint on `results`.\n2. The **weights** that map a tier to a health-score penalty determine how\n   historical results aggregate. Once results are written and trends are drawn,\n   re-weighting silently rewrites the meaning of every past data point. The\n   roadmap calls this out explicitly: *\"This affects the DB schema for run\n   results and cannot be changed cheaply after data is written.\"*\n\nThe open question this ADR closes: **what are the weights, and what is the\nhealth-score formula** — so the Week-6 dashboard and the Week-8 result-service\ntests have a fixed target, and the Week-3 migration writes the right CHECK.\n\n## Decision\n\n**Adopt four ordered severity tiers with fixed penalty weights, and a single\nnormalised health-score formula that is SQL-aggregatable.**\n\n### Tiers and weights\n\n| Status | Penalty weight | Meaning | Alert behaviour (Week 6) |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| `pass` | `0.0` | check met its expectation | none |\n| `warn` | `0.5` | soft threshold breached — flag only | quiet (no @mention) |\n| `fail` | `1.0` | check failed | standard alert |\n| `critical` | `2.0` | failed past the critical threshold | urgent (@channel) |\n\nWeights are **not** stored per-result. Only the `status` string is persisted;\nthe weight is a fixed lookup applied at aggregation time. This keeps the weights\nre-tunable in code *for forward-looking display* without a data migration — but\nthe **tier a result was assigned** is immutable history (it is what the\nthresholds evaluated to at run time).\n\n### Health-score formula\n\nFor any set of N check results in scope (a suite, an env, a time window):\n\n```\npenalty(status) = {pass:0.0, warn:0.5, fail:1.0, critical:2.0}\n\nhealth_score = 100 × (1 − Σ penalty(statusᵢ) / (N × W_max))   where W_max = 2.0\n```\n\n- Range is a clean `[0, 100]`: all-`pass` → 100, all-`critical` → 0,\n  all-`fail` → 50, all-`warn` → 75.\n- `W_max = 2.0` (the `critical` weight) is the normaliser, so a suite that is\n  entirely `fail` still scores above the floor — `critical` is meaningfully\n  worse than `fail`, not collapsed to the same 0.\n- It is a pure `SUM(...)/COUNT(*)` over the persisted `status` column → computes\n  in one SQL pass for any filter (env / datasource / suite / date range), no\n  per-check application code. This is the same aggregation discipline as the\n  `metric_value` numeric column (ADR 0012): the dashboard never reduces JSONB\n  in Python.\n\n### Binary fallback\n\nA check with no tier thresholds set behaves as plain pass/fail: it resolves to\n`pass` (penalty 0) or `fail` (penalty 1.0). `warn` and `critical` are simply\nnever assigned. The formula is unchanged — binary checks are the N-tier formula\nwith two of four tiers unused.\n\n## Consequences\n\n**Positive**\n- Week-3 migration writes a settled `status` CHECK (`pass | warn | fail |\n  critical`); no re-migration when the dashboard lands.\n- Week-6 health score and Week-8 result-service tests have an exact, testable\n  target (e.g. `{fail, fail, pass, pass}` → 75.0).\n- Weights live in one constant, aggregation is one SQL expression — severity-aware\n  alert routing reads the same `status` column.\n\n**Negative**\n- Weights (0.5 / 1.0 / 2.0) are a judgement call, not derived from data. Accepted:\n  they are display-time weights, re-tunable in code without touching stored\n  history; only the *tier assignment* is immutable.\n- A single global health score can mask a single catastrophic table inside an\n  otherwise-green suite. Mitigated by the per-suite / per-check breakdowns the\n  dashboard renders alongside the headline number (Week 6).\n\n## Alternatives considered\n\n- **Normalise by `W_max = 1.0` (the `fail` weight), clamp at 0.** All-`fail` → 0,\n  all-`critical` → 0 (clamped). Rejected: collapses the fail/critical distinction\n  at the aggregate floor, which is exactly the signal critical exists to carry.\n- **Store the weight on each result row.** Rejected: bloats `results`, and makes\n  a weight change a data migration instead of a constant edit, while gaining\n  nothing the status string + lookup doesn't already give.\n- **Binary pass/fail only for v1, tiers later.** Rejected: tiers are a Week-3\n  roadmap deliverable and the threshold columns ride the one-shot Week-3 schema\n  migration (ADR 0012). Adding `warn`/`critical` to the `status` CHECK later is a\n  second backward-compat two-step — the precise retrofit this ADR exists to avoid.\n- **Continuous severity (0.0–1.0 float per result) instead of four tiers.**\n  Rejected for v1: no UI affordance to author a continuous severity, and alert\n  routing needs discrete buckets anyway. The numeric `metric_value` (ADR 0012)\n  already preserves the underlying scalar for anyone who wants finer analysis.\n\n## Related\n\n- ADR 0012 — monitor-kind seam (`check.kind` + `metric_value` / `duration_ms`);\n  **rides the same Week-3 migration** as the threshold/status columns.\n- `docs/progress.md` — Week 3 \"Severity threshold tiers\" tasks; Week 6 health\n  score + severity-aware alert routing; Week 8 result-service tests.\n- `context/DataQ_platform_roadmap.md` — Week 3 severity tiers; post-v1 Theme A\n  (auto-monitors emit the same tiers over `metric_value`).\n- CLAUDE.md §9 (decision table), §5 (monitor-kind seam).\n"
}

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/docs/adr/0012-monitor-kind-seam.md",
  "content": "# ADR 0012 — Monitor-kind seam (`check.kind` discriminator + numeric metric storage)\n\n- **Status:** Accepted\n- **Date:** 2026-05-30\n- **Deciders:** @TheurgicDuke771\n\n## Context\n\nEvery v1 check is a Great Expectations expectation (ADR 0003): a value-level\nassertion on column/table data. But most real data-quality incidents are **not**\nvalue-level — they are **freshness** (a table stopped loading) and **volume** (a\nload delivered 10% of its usual rows). These are *monitors over a measured\nscalar*, not expectations over row values. The post-v1 roadmap (Theme A) makes\nthis the leap from \"a GX runner\" to \"a DQ platform\": freshness, volume,\nschema-drift, and anomaly auto-monitors.\n\nv1 will **not** build those monitors. But the v1 check/result schema is written\nin the Week-3 migration, and that migration is a **one-shot** for schema seams\n(CLAUDE.md §10) — once results are written, changing the shape is a\nbackward-compatible two-step deploy (W5+ discipline). If v1 ships a schema that\nassumes \"a check is always a GX expectation, a result is always binary + a JSONB\n`observed_value`,\" then every auto-monitor in v1.x forces a check/result schema\nrewrite that ripples into the suite, check, run, and result layers.\n\nTwo specific gaps:\n\n1. **No discriminator on `checks`.** The run path hardwires \"expectation → GX.\"\n   A freshness monitor has no expectation_type; it has an interval and a\n   timestamp column. Without a `kind`, there's nowhere to branch on *what kind of\n   monitor this is* (a question orthogonal to *which datasource* — that's the\n   `CheckRunner` / `ConnectionAdapter` seam).\n2. **Metrics only live in JSONB `observed_value`.** A freshness monitor measures\n   \"hours since last load = 26.5\"; a volume monitor measures \"row count =\n   1,203,847.\" These are scalars you must `AVG()` / `STDDEV()` for Week-6 trend\n   charts and v1.1 anomaly baselines. **You cannot aggregate a value buried in a\n   JSONB blob in SQL** — the dashboard would have to pull every row and reduce in\n   Python.\n\nThis decision must land **before the Week-3 threshold migration** so both\ncolumns ride that single migration.\n\n## Decision\n\n**Add the monitor-kind seam in v1 — schema + dispatch only — and implement\n`expectation` as the sole live kind. Reserve the other kinds; do not build them.**\n\nThis seam is **orthogonal** to the datasource seams (`CheckRunner`,\n`ConnectionAdapter`, ADR 0011): those vary behaviour by *datasource type*; this\nvaries by *monitor kind*. A freshness monitor on Snowflake and a freshness\nmonitor on Unity Catalog are the same `kind`, different `CheckRunner`.\n\n### 1. `check.kind` discriminator (schema)\n\n- Add `kind TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'expectation'` to `checks`, with a CHECK\n  constraint over `('expectation', 'freshness', 'volume', 'schema_drift',\n  'anomaly')`.\n- v1 only ever writes `'expectation'`. The other four are **reserved**:\n  constraint-valid so a v1.x monitor is a pure additive row, but no code produces\n  or consumes them yet.\n- Kind-specific parameters reuse the existing `checks.config` JSONB (a freshness\n  monitor stores `{column, interval_hours}` there) — no per-kind columns.\n\n### 2. Run-path dispatch by `kind`\n\n- The run path dispatches on `check.kind`: `'expectation'` → the GX `CheckRunner`\n  (existing path); any other kind raises `NotImplementedError` until its v1.x\n  impl lands.\n- This is a `match`/dispatch at the same layer that already selects the\n  `CheckRunner` by `connection.type` (the Week-5 generic dispatch, ADR 0011) —\n  the two dispatches compose (`kind` chooses the *monitor*, `connection.type`\n  chooses the *adapter*). v1 has exactly one cell of that matrix populated.\n\n### 3. Numeric metric storage (schema)\n\n- Add to `results`:\n  - `metric_value NUMERIC NULL` — the SQL-aggregatable scalar the monitor\n    measured. For an `expectation`, this is the natural numeric the check yields\n    where one exists (e.g. unexpected-row count / percent); NULL where a check\n    has no meaningful scalar. For freshness/volume/anomaly (v1.x) it is *the*\n    measurement.\n  - `duration_ms INT NULL` — per-check runtime, for the Week-6 cost/perf surface\n    (post-v1 Theme E).\n- **`metric_value` is the aggregatable mirror of `observed_value`, not a\n  replacement.** Rich/structured detail stays in JSONB `observed_value`; the one\n  scalar worth trending/baselining is *also* written to `metric_value` so Week-6\n  trends and v1.1 anomaly baselines are a `SELECT AVG(metric_value) ...` — never\n  a JSONB reduction in Python (same discipline as the health-score SQL in\n  ADR 0005).\n\n## Consequences\n\n**Positive**\n- v1.x auto-monitors (freshness, volume, schema-drift, anomaly — Theme A) slot in\n  as a new `kind` value + a new dispatch branch + a `CheckRunner`-style monitor\n  impl. **No check / result / suite schema rewrite, no second two-step migration.**\n- Week-6 trend charts and v1.1 anomaly baselines read one indexed NUMERIC column.\n- The seam is ~two columns + one CHECK + one dispatch branch — almost free,\n  because the Week-3 migration is being written anyway.\n\n**Negative**\n- `metric_value` is nullable and, for v1 expectations, often redundant with\n  `observed_value`. Accepted: a nullable NUMERIC is cheap, and the redundancy is\n  the whole point — one column is aggregatable, the JSONB is not.\n- A reserved CHECK value set that v1 never emits looks like dead schema. Accepted\n  and documented here: it is deliberate forward-compat, not an oversight.\n\n## Alternatives considered\n\n- **Defer the whole seam to v1.x.** Rejected: the check/result schema is written\n  now; adding `kind` + `metric_value` after results exist is a backward-compat\n  two-step that ripples through the check/result/suite layer — the exact retrofit\n  CLAUDE.md §10 flags as a one-shot to avoid.\n- **Store metrics only in JSONB `observed_value`.** Rejected: not SQL-aggregatable.\n  Week-6 trends and anomaly baselines would pull every result row and reduce in\n  app code, which doesn't scale and duplicates logic the DB does in one pass.\n- **Build the freshness/volume monitors in v1.** Rejected: net-new scope, not in\n  the 8-week plan, and GX-only (ADR 0003) means each is a non-GX monitor impl.\n  Only the *seam* is built now; the monitors are post-v1 Theme A.\n- **A separate `metrics` table keyed by result.** Rejected for v1: a join for one\n  scalar per result, when a nullable column on `results` is simpler and indexes\n  the same. Revisit only if a single result needs many named metrics.\n- **Model `kind` as a separate per-kind check table (table-per-kind).** Rejected:\n  multiplies the CRUD/seam surface; the JSONB `config` + a discriminator column\n  already carries kind-specific params without new tables.\n\n## Related\n\n- ADR 0003 — GX-only for v1 (why non-expectation kinds are reserved, not built;\n  DQX/streaming boundary).\n- ADR 0005 — severity tier weights; **rides the same Week-3 migration** and shares\n  the SQL-aggregation discipline (`status` rollup ↔ `metric_value` trends).\n- ADR 0011 — datasource extensibility seams (`CheckRunner` by `connection.type`);\n  the dispatch this composes with. `kind` ⟂ datasource.\n- `docs/progress.md` — Week 3 \"Monitor abstraction & metric storage\" tasks.\n- `context/DataQ_platform_roadmap.md` — post-v1 Theme A (auto-monitors).\n- CLAUDE.md §5 (monitor-kind seam), §10 (Week-3 one-shot migration).\n"
}
```

Everything's in place to plan PR 6 precisely. Here's what I found that shapes the work:

**The API + service layers are already fully generic.** [connections.py](backend/app/api/v1/connections.py) dispatches every verb (create/list/get/update/delete/test) by the `type` string through the registry — it never branches on type. [connection_service.py](backend/app/services/connection_service.py) is type-agnostic too. So **PR 6 touches almost no existing code**: it's a new adapter + a registry line + a migration + a small tweak to disambiguate the conflict error.

## Proposed PR 6 plan — ADF connection CRUD + `(type, env)` guard

**1. ADF connection adapter** (new file) — implements the existing `ConnectionAdapter` Protocol from [datasources/base.py:77](backend/app/datasources/base.py#L77):
- `ADFConfig` (pydantic, `extra="forbid"`): `subscription_id`, `resource_group`, `factory_name`, `tenant_id`, `client_id`. Secret=[REDACTED] `client_secret`.
- `validate_config()` → parse/validate; `test()` → service-principal connectivity check.

**2. `(type, env)` uniqueness guard (#72)** — Alembic migration adding a **partial unique index**:
```sql
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_connections_orchestrator_type_env
  ON connections (type, env) WHERE type IN ('adf','airflow')
```
This is the right shape: DB-enforced, additive (backward-compatible), and leaves datasources alone (Snowflake DEV can still have N connections per env). I'd include `airflow` in the predicate now so its CRUD task later needs no second migration.

**3. Service tweak** — [connection_service.py:113](backend/app/services/connection_service.py#L113) currently maps *every* `IntegrityError` to "name already exists." Branch on the constraint name so the orchestrator-uniqueness violation returns a distinct 409 ("an {adf} connection already exists for env {qa}").

**4. Registry** — one line in [registry.py:19](backend/app/datasources/registry.py#L19).

**5. Tests** (PR 5 shipped tests, so this should too): adapter validation; service-level guard (2nd ADF in env → 409, ADF in another env OK, 2 Snowflakes same env still OK); API create/duplicate/list-filter.

**Out of scope** (kept honest): Airflow CRUD, the ADF *webhook receiver* (separate Week-2 task), and `secret_ref`-required enforcement (tracked as the #41 nit).

Two genuine decisions before I start:

44	class SnowflakeConfig(BaseModel):
45	    """Non-secret Snowflake connection config (the password comes from secrets).
46	
47	    Maps from ``Connection.config``. ``schema`` is aliased to ``schema_`` to
48	    avoid shadowing pydantic's ``BaseModel.schema``.
49	    """
50	
51	    model_config = ConfigDict(populate_by_name=True, extra="forbid")
52	
53	    account: str
54	    user: str
55	    database: str
56	    schema_: str = Field(alias="schema")
57	    warehouse: str
58	    role: str | None = None
59	
60	
61	def build_connection_string(config: SnowflakeConfig, password: str) -> str:
62	    """Assemble a snowflake-sqlalchemy URL. User/password/params are URL-encoded."""
63	    params = {"warehouse": config.warehouse}
64	    if config.role:
65	        params["role"] = config.role
66	    query = "&".join(f"{key}={quote_plus(value)}" for key, value in params.items())
67	    return (
68	        f"snowflake://{quote_plus(config.user)}:{quote_plus(password)}"
69	        f"@{config.account}/{config.database}/{config.schema_}?{query}"
70	    )
71	
72	
73	def _expectation_class_name(expectation_type: str) -> str:
74	    """snake_case GX type → PascalCase class name.
75	
76	    ``expect_column_values_to_not_be_null`` → ``ExpectColumnValuesToNotBeNull``.
77	    """
78	    return "".join(part.title() for part in expectation_type.split("_"))
79	
80	
81	def _to_gx_expectation(spec: CheckSpec) -> Any:
82	    class_name = _expectation_class_name(spec.expectation_type)
83	    expectation_cls = getattr(gxe, class_name, None)
84	    if expectation_cls is None:
85	        raise UnknownExpectationError(
86	            f"Unknown expectation_type {spec.expectation_type!r} (no gx class {class_name!r})"
87	        )
88	    return expectation_cls(**spec.kwargs)
89	
90	
91	def _extract_sample_failures(result: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
92	    sample = {key: result[key] for key in _SAMPLE_KEYS if key in result}
93	    return sample or None
94	
95	
96	def _expected_value(kwargs: Any) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
97	    cleaned = {key: value for key, value in dict(kwargs).items() if key not in _GX_INTERNAL_KWARGS}
98	    return cleaned or None
99	
100	
101	def to_suite_outcome(gx_result: Any) -> SuiteOutcome:
102	    """Map a GX ExpectationSuiteValidationResult onto our GX-agnostic DTO.
103	
104	    Kept module-level (not a private method) so it is unit-testable with a
105	    constructed GX result, no Snowflake connection required.
106	    """
107	    outcomes: list[CheckOutcome] = []
108	    for check_result in gx_result.results:
109	        config = check_result.expectation_config
110	        detail: dict[str, Any] = check_result.result or {}
111	        observed = (
112	            {"observed_value": detail["observed_value"]} if "observed_value" in detail else None
113	        )
114	        outcomes.append(
115	            CheckOutcome(
116	                expectation_type=config.type,
117	                success=bool(check_result.success),
118	                observed_value=observed,
119	                expected_value=_expected_value(config.kwargs) if config.kwargs else None,
120	                sample_failures=_extract_sample_failures(detail),
121	            )
122	        )
123	    return SuiteOutcome(success=bool(gx_result.success), checks=outcomes)
124

127	    """`CheckRunner` for Snowflake. Building the asset connects to the warehouse."""
128	
129	    def __init__(self, config: SnowflakeConfig, password: str) -> None:
130	        self._config = config
131	        self._connection_string = build_connection_string(config, password)

133	    def run_checks(
134	        self,
135	        *,
136	        table: str,
137	        schema: str | None,
138	        checks: list[CheckSpec],
139	    ) -> SuiteOutcome:
140	        context = gx.get_context(mode="ephemeral")
141	        datasource = context.data_sources.add_snowflake(
142	            name=f"sf-{table}",
143	            connection_string=self._connection_string,
144	        )
145	        asset = datasource.add_table_asset(
146	            name=table,
147	            table_name=table,
148	            schema_name=schema or self._config.schema_,
149	        )
150	        batch_definition = asset.add_batch_definition_whole_table(name="whole_table")
151	        # GX 1.17 requires the suite and validation definition to be registered
152	        # on the context before run(); a free-standing ValidationDefinition.run()
153	        # raises ValidationDefinitionRelatedResourcesFreshnessError. The context
154	        # is ephemeral (per-run), so the fixed names never collide across runs.
155	        suite = context.suites.add(
156	            gx.ExpectationSuite(
157	                name=f"suite-{table}",
158	                expectations=[_to_gx_expectation(check) for check in checks],
159	            )
160	        )
161	        validation_definition = context.validation_definitions.add(
162	            gx.ValidationDefinition(
163	                name=f"vd-{table}",
164	                data=batch_definition,
165	                suite=suite,
166	            )
167	        )
168	        result = validation_definition.run(result_format="COMPLETE")
169	        return to_suite_outcome(result)

172	def build_snowflake_runner(
173	    *,
174	    config: dict[str, Any],
175	    secret_ref: str | None,
176	    secret_store: SecretStore,
177	) -> SnowflakeCheckRunner:
178	    """Build a runner from a `Connection` row's config + secret_ref.
179	
180	    Takes primitives (not the ORM model) to keep the adapter decoupled from the
181	    DB layer.
182	    """
183	    if not secret_ref:
184	        raise ValueError("Snowflake connection requires secret_ref for the password")
185	    sf_config = SnowflakeConfig.model_validate(config)
186	    password = secret_store.get(secret_ref)
187	    return SnowflakeCheckRunner(sf_config, password)

{
  "file_path": "/Users/arijit/Coding/Python/DataQ/backend/app/orchestration/adf.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"Azure Data Factory connection adapter (orchestration provider, not a datasource).\n\nADF is an orchestration provider (CLAUDE.md §4): DataQ monitors its pipeline\nruns and triggers suites on success — it is never a queryable datasource, so\nthis module implements only the `ConnectionAdapter` seam (config validation +\nconnectivity test), never `CheckRunner`.\n\nThe connection identifies one data factory (subscription / resource group /\nfactory) and authenticates with an Azure AD service principal — `client_id` in\nconfig, the SP `client_secret` in the SecretStore. ``test`` proves both: it\nacquires a service-principal token (OAuth2 client-credentials) and GETs the\nfactory through the ARM REST API, so a green test means the credentials are\nvalid *and* the named factory is reachable. It uses ``httpx`` only — no Azure\nSDK dependency — and, like the Snowflake adapter, runs live but fails-soft\npending real credentials (the connection-service test path wraps and never\nechoes the adapter exception, so tokens/secrets can't leak to the client).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom typing import Any\n\nimport httpx\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict\n\n# Azure AD token endpoint + ARM management host. The client-credentials grant\n# against this scope yields a bearer token usable for the factory GET below.\n_AAD_TOKEN_URL = \"https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant_id}/oauth2/v2.0/token\"\n_ARM_SCOPE = \"https://management.azure.com/.default\"\n_ARM_FACTORY_URL = (\n    \"https://management.azure.com/subscriptions/{subscription_id}\"\n    \"/resourceGroups/{resource_group}\"\n    \"/providers/Microsoft.DataFactory/factories/{factory_name}\"\n)\n_ARM_API_VERSION = \"2018-06-01\"\n\n# Fail fast rather than hang the request thread on an unreachable endpoint.\n_TEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 10.0\n\n\nclass ADFConfig(BaseModel):\n    \"\"\"Non-secret ADF connection config (the SP client secret comes from secrets).\n\n    Maps from ``Connection.config``. Identifies one data factory plus the service\n    principal's non-secret half (`tenant_id` / `client_id`); the `client_secret`\n    is resolved from the SecretStore at test time and never stored here.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    model_config = ConfigDict(extra=\"forbid\")\n\n    subscription_id: str\n    resource_group: str\n    factory_name: str\n    tenant_id: str\n    client_id: str\n\n\ndef _acquire_token(config: ADFConfig, client_secret: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"OAuth2 client-credentials token for the ARM management scope.\"\"\"\n    response = httpx.post(\n        _AAD_TOKEN_URL.format(tenant_id=config.tenant_id),\n        data={\n            \"grant_type\": \"client_credentials\",\n            \"client_id\": config.client_id,\n            \"client_secret\": client_secret,\n            \"scope\": _ARM_SCOPE,\n        },\n        timeout=_TEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,\n    )\n    response.raise_for_status()\n    token = response.json().get(\"access_token\")\n    if not token:\n        raise ValueError(\"Azure AD token response contained no access_token\")\n    return str(token)\n\n\nclass ADFConnectionAdapter:\n    \"\"\"`ConnectionAdapter` for Azure Data Factory — config validation + live test.\"\"\"\n\n    def validate_config(self, raw: dict[str, Any]) -> ADFConfig:\n        return ADFConfig.model_validate(raw)\n\n    def test(self, raw: dict[str, Any], secret: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Acquire an SP token and GET the factory; raise on any failure.\n\n        ``secret`` is the service-principal client secret. A successful return\n        means the SP authenticated AND the named factory is reachable.\n        \"\"\"\n        config = self.validate_config(raw)\n        token = _acquire_token(config, secret)\n        response = httpx.get(\n            _ARM_FACTORY_URL.format(\n                subscription_id=config.subscription_id,\n                resource_group=config.resource_group,\n                factory_name=config.factory_name,\n            ),\n            params={\"api-version\": _ARM_API_VERSION},\n            headers={\"Authorization\": f\"Bearer {token}\"},\n            timeout=_TEST_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,\n        )\n        response.raise_for_status()\n"
}

Distinguished from the\n# (name, env) unique constraint so each violation gets an accurate 409 message.\n_ORCHESTRATOR_UNIQUE_INDEX = \"uq_connections_orchestrator_type_env\"\n\n\ndef _conflict_from_integrity_error(\n    exc: IntegrityError, *, conn_type: str, env: str\n) -> ConnectionConflictError:\n    \"\"\"Map a unique-violation to the right 409, by which constraint fired.\n\n    Postgres surfaces the violated constraint/index name on the driver\n    exception's ``diag``; use it to tell the orchestrator (type, env) singleton\n    breach apart from a duplicate (name, env).\n    \"\"\"\n    diag = getattr(getattr(exc, \"orig\", None), \"diag\", None)\n    constraint_name = getattr(diag, \"constraint_name\", None)\n    if constraint_name == _ORCHESTRATOR_UNIQUE_INDEX:\n        return ConnectionConflictError(\n            f\"an orchestration connection of type {conn_type!r} already exists in env {env!r}\",\n            detail={\"type\": conn_type, \"env\": env},\n        )\n    return ConnectionConflictError(\n        \"a connection with this name already exists in this env\",\n        detail={\"type\": conn_type, \"env\": env},\n    )"

130	+- Weights (0.5 / 1.0 / 2.0) are a judgement call, not derived from data. Accepted:
131	+  they are display-time weights, re-tunable in code without touching stored
132	+  history; only the *tier assignment* is immutable.
133	+- A single global health score can mask a single catastrophic table inside an
134	+  otherwise-green suite. Mitigated by the per-suite / per-check breakdowns the
135	+  dashboard renders alongside the headline number (Week 6).
136	+
137	+## Alternatives considered
138	+
139	+- **Normalise by `W_max = 1.0` (the `fail` weight), clamp at 0.** All-`fail` → 0,
140	+  all-`critical` → 0 (clamped). Rejected: collapses the fail/critical distinction
141	+  at the aggregate floor, which is exactly the signal critical exists to carry.
142	+- **Store the weight on each result row.** Rejected: bloats `results`, and makes
143	+  a weight change a data migration instead of a constant edit, while gaining
144	+  nothing the status string + lookup doesn't already give.
145	+- **Binary pass/fail only for v1, tiers later.** Rejected: tiers are a Week-3
146	+  roadmap deliverable and the threshold columns ride the one-shot Week-3 schema
147	+  migration (ADR 0012). Adding `warn`/`critical` to the `status` CHECK later is a
148	+  second backward-compat two-step — the precise retrofit this ADR exists to avoid.
149	+- **Continuous severity (0.0–1.0 float per result) instead of four tiers.**
150	+  Rejected for v1: no UI affordance to author a continuous severity, and alert
151	+  routing needs discrete buckets anyway. The numeric `metric_value` (ADR 0012)
152	+  already preserves the underlying scalar for anyone who wants finer analysis.
153	+
154	+## Related
155	+
156	+- ADR 0012 — monitor-kind seam (`check.kind` + `metric_value` / `duration_ms`);
157	+  **rides the same Week-3 migration** as the threshold/status columns.
158	+- `docs/progress.md` — Week 3 "Severity threshold tiers" tasks; Week 6 health
159	+  score + severity-aware alert routing; Week 8 result-service tests.

161	+  (auto-monitors emit the same tiers over `metric_value`).

164	new file mode 100644

167	+++ b/docs/adr/0012-monitor-kind-seam.md
168	@@ -0,0 +1,136 @@
169	+# ADR 0012 — Monitor-kind seam (`check.kind` discriminator + numeric metric storage)
170	+
171	+- **Status:** Accepted
172	+- **Date:** 2026-05-30
173	+- **Deciders:** @TheurgicDuke771
174	+
175	+## Context
176	+
177	+Every v1 check is a Great Expectations expectation (ADR 0003): a value-level
178	+assertion on column/table data. But most real data-quality incidents are **not**
179	+value-level — they are **freshness** (a table stopped loading) and **volume** (a
180	+load delivered 10% of its usual rows). These are *monitors over a measured
181	+scalar*, not expectations over row values. The post-v1 roadmap (Theme A) makes
182	+this the leap from "a GX runner" to "a DQ platform": freshness, volume,
183	+schema-drift, and anomaly auto-monitors.
184	+
185	+v1 will **not** build those monitors. But the v1 check/result schema is written
186	+in the Week-3 migration, and that migration is a **one-shot** for schema seams
187	+(CLAUDE.md §10) — once results are written, changing the shape is a
188	+backward-compatible two-step deploy (W5+ discipline). If v1 ships a schema that
189	+assumes "a check is always a GX expectation, a result is always binary + a JSONB
190	+`observed_value`," then every auto-monitor in v1.x forces a check/result schema
191	+rewrite that ripples into the suite, check, run, and result layers.
192	+
193	+Two specific gaps:
194	+
195	+1. **No discriminator on `checks`.** The run path hardwires "expectation → GX."
196	+   A freshness monitor has no expectation_type; it has an interval and a
197	+   timestamp column. Without a `kind`, there's nowhere to branch on *what kind of
198	+   monitor this is* (a question orthogonal to *which datasource* — that's the
199	+   `CheckRunner` / `ConnectionAdapter` seam).
200	+2. **Metrics only live in JSONB `observed_value`.** A freshness monitor measures
201	+   "hours since last load = 26.5"; a volume monitor measures "row count =
202	+   1,203,847." These are scalars you must `AVG()` / `STDDEV()` for Week-6 trend
203	+   charts and v1.1 anomaly baselines. **You cannot aggregate a value buried in a
204	+   JSONB blob in SQL** — the dashboard would have to pull every row and reduce in
205	+   Python.
206	+
207	+This decision must land **before the Week-3 threshold migration** so both
208	+columns ride that single migration.
209	+
210	+## Decision
211	+
212	+**Add the monitor-kind seam in v1 — schema + dispatch only — and implement
213	+`expectation` as the sole live kind. Reserve the other kinds; do not build them.**
214	+
215	+This seam is **orthogonal** to the datasource seams (`CheckRunner`,
216	+`ConnectionAdapter`, ADR 0011): those vary behaviour by *datasource type*; this
217	+varies by *monitor kind*. A freshness monitor on Snowflake and a freshness
218	+monitor on Unity Catalog are the same `kind`, different `CheckRunner`.
219	+
220	+### 1. `check.kind` discriminator (schema)
221	+
222	+- Add `kind TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'expectation'` to `checks`, with a CHECK
223	+  constraint over `('expectation', 'freshness', 'volume', 'schema_drift',
224	+  'anomaly')`.
225	+- v1 only ever writes `'expectation'`. The other four are **reserved**:
226	+  constraint-valid so a v1.x monitor is a pure additive row, but no code produces
227	+  or consumes them yet.
228	+- Kind-specific parameters reuse the existing `checks.config` JSONB (a freshness
229	+  monitor stores `{column, interval_hours}` there) — no per-kind columns.
230	+
231	+### 2. Run-path dispatch by `kind`
232	+
233	+- The run path dispatches on `check.kind`: `'expectation'` → the GX `CheckRunner`
234	+  (existing path); any other kind raises `NotImplementedError` until its v1.x
235	+  impl lands.
236	+- This is a `match`/dispatch at the same layer that already selects the
237	+  `CheckRunner` by `connection.type` (the Week-5 generic dispatch, ADR 0011) —
238	+  the two dispatches compose (`kind` chooses the *monitor*, `connection.type`
239	+  chooses the *adapter*). v1 has exactly one cell of that matrix populated.
240	+
241	+### 3. Numeric metric storage (schema)
242	+
243	+- Add to `results`:
244	+  - `metric_value NUMERIC NULL` — the SQL-aggregatable scalar the monitor
245	+    measured. For an `expectation`, this is the natural numeric the check yields
246	+    where one exists (e.g. unexpected-row count / percent); NULL where a check
247	+    has no meaningful scalar. For freshness/volume/anomaly (v1.x) it is *the*
248	+    measurement.
249	+  - `duration_ms INT NULL` — per-check runtime, for the Week-6 cost/perf surface
250	+    (post-v1 Theme E).
251	+- **`metric_value` is the aggregatable mirror of `observed_value`, not a
252	+  replacement.** Rich/structured detail stays in JSONB `observed_value`; the one
253	+  scalar worth trending/baselining is *also* written to `metric_value` so Week-6
254	+  trends and v1.1 anomaly baselines are a `SELECT AVG(metric_value) ...` — never
255	+  a JSONB reduction in Python (same discipline as the health-score SQL in
256	+  ADR 0005).
257	+
258	+## Consequences
259	+
260	+**Positive**
261	+- v1.x auto-monitors (freshness, volume, schema-drift, anomaly — Theme A) slot in
262	+  as a new `kind` value + a new dispatch branch + a `CheckRunner`-style monitor
263	+  impl. **No check / result / suite schema rewrite, no second two-step migration.**
264	+- Week-6 trend charts and v1.1 anomaly baselines read one indexed NUMERIC column.
265	+- The seam is ~two columns + one CHECK + one dispatch branch — almost free,
266	+  because the Week-3 migration is being written anyway.
267	+
268	+**Negative**
269	+- `metric_value` is nullable and, for v1 expectations, often redundant with
270	+  `observed_value`. Accepted: a nullable NUMERIC is cheap, and the redundancy is
271	+  the whole point — one column is aggregatable, the JSONB is not.
272	+- A reserved CHECK value set that v1 never emits looks like dead schema. Accepted
273	+  and documented here: it is deliberate forward-compat, not an oversight.
274	+
275	+## Alternatives considered
276	+
277	+- **Defer the whole seam to v1.x.** Rejected: the check/result schema is written
278	+  now; adding `kind` + `metric_value` after results exist is a backward-compat
279	+  two-step that ripples through the check/result/suite layer — the exact retrofit
280	+  CLAUDE.md §10 flags as a one-shot to avoid.
281	+- **Store metrics only in JSONB `observed_value`.** Rejected: not SQL-aggregatable.
282	+  Week-6 trends and anomaly baselines would pull every result row and reduce in
283	+  app code, which doesn't scale and duplicates logic the DB does in one pass.
284	+- **Build the freshness/volume monitors in v1.** Rejected: net-new scope, not in
285	+  the 8-week plan, and GX-only (ADR 0003) means each is a non-GX monitor impl.
286	+  Only the *seam* is built now; the monitors are post-v1 Theme A.
287	+- **A separate `metrics` table keyed by result.** Rejected for v1: a join for one
288	+  scalar per result, when a nullable column on `results` is simpler and indexes
289	+  the same. Revisit only if a single result needs many named metrics.
290	+- **Model `kind` as a separate per-kind check table (table-per-kind).** Rejected:
291	+  multiplies the CRUD/seam surface; the JSONB `config` + a discriminator column
292	+  already carries kind-specific params without new tables.
293	+

1	# ADR 0006 — ADF webhook authentication (shared secret + hard-cutover rotation)
2	
3	- **Status:** Accepted
4	- **Date:** 2026-05-30
5	- **Deciders:** @TheurgicDuke771
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	Per [ADR 0004](0004-orchestration-abstraction.md), Azure Data Factory (ADF) pipeline run events reach DataQ via an Azure Monitor alert rule that POSTs to `POST /api/v1/orchestration/events/adf`. We must authenticate these inbound requests so a third party cannot forge pipeline events (which can trigger suite runs on successful-completion bindings).
10	
11	The transport is constrained by Azure Monitor itself:
12	
13	- A **plain action-group webhook cannot attach arbitrary custom headers**. So a signed `X-DataQ-Signature`-style header (as used for Airflow in [ADR 0007](0007-airflow-callback-model.md)) is not directly available without an intermediary.
14	- Azure Monitor's **Secure Webhook** action uses an Azure AD bearer token, which is stronger but requires an additional app registration + AAD wiring and shifts away from the shared-secret model framed in ADR 0004.
15	
16	## Decision
17	
18	**Authenticate the ADF webhook with a shared secret carried as a URL query parameter, validated constant-time against a single secret stored in Key Vault. Rotate by hard cutover. No request-freshness check in v1.**
19	
20	### Authentication
21	
22	- Azure Monitor posts to `https://<api-host>/api/v1/orchestration/events/adf?token=<secret>` over **HTTPS only**.
23	- The endpoint reads `token`, compares it **constant-time** (`hmac.compare_digest`) against the secret resolved from Key Vault.
24	- Missing / mismatched token → **401**. The token is never logged (PII/secret redaction at the logger level, per CLAUDE.md §10).
25	- After successful auth, the endpoint returns **200 for all well-formed events** — including non-success and ignored events — so Azure Monitor does not enter a retry storm. Malformed body → 422.
26	
27	### Secret storage & config
28	
29	- Secret lives in Key Vault, surfaced to the app as `ADF_WEBHOOK_SECRET` via the existing `SecretStore` abstraction (PR 3b) — never inlined in config or committed.
30	- The same value is configured on the Azure Monitor action group's webhook URL.
31	
32	### Rotation — hard cutover
33	
34	- **One active secret at a time.** Rotation = update the Key Vault secret **and** the Azure Monitor action-group webhook URL in lockstep.
35	- A brief mismatch window during rotation may drop a webhook delivery; this is **acceptable because the 10-minute ADF REST polling fallback** (ADR 0004) recovers any missed `succeeded` runs. No dual-secret overlap logic in v1.
36	
37	### Replay / freshness — not enforced in v1
38	
39	- v1 validates the shared secret only; it does **not** reject stale `firedDateTime` timestamps.
40	- Duplicate or replayed deliveries are neutralised downstream by the **idempotent upsert keyed on (`provider`, `provider_run_id`)** in `pipeline_runs` — a replayed event updates the same row and does not re-trigger a suite run.
41	- Freshness enforcement is a documented hardening candidate, deferred until replay is shown to be a real risk.
42	
43	## Consequences
44	
45	**Positive**
46	- Minimal infra — no extra Azure AD app registration, no Logic App hop. Ships inside the Week 2 webhook-receiver PR.
47	- Constant-time compare + HTTPS-only + idempotent upsert covers the realistic threat model for a single-tenant v1.
48	- Rotation is operationally simple; the polling fallback already exists as the safety net.
49	
50	**Negative**
51	- The secret appears in the webhook **URL**, so it can surface in Azure Monitor action-group config and potentially some network/proxy logs. Mitigated by HTTPS, treating it as a rotatable credential, and never logging the query string on our side. A header- or AAD-based scheme would avoid this but at higher infra cost (see Alternatives).
52	- Hard cutover can drop deliveries during the rotation window; accepted because polling backfills.
53	- No replay window means a captured valid request could be replayed; impact is bounded to idempotent no-ops on existing `pipeline_runs` rows (no double-trigger).
54	
55	## Alternatives considered
56	
57	- **Secure Webhook (Azure AD bearer token)** — rejected for v1. Strongest option and avoids secret-in-URL, but costs an extra app registration + AAD validation path and revises ADR 0004's shared-secret framing. Revisit if the security review before Week 7 deploy flags secret-in-URL as unacceptable.
58	- **Logic App intermediary that injects a signed header** — rejected. Would let ADF and Airflow share an `X-DataQ-Signature` HMAC design (symmetric), but adds a Logic App resource + an operational hop to pay for and monitor.
59	- **Dual-secret overlap rotation** — rejected for v1. Zero-downtime rotation, but the polling fallback already covers the small cutover gap, so the extra validation branch isn't worth it yet.
60	
61	## Related
62	
63	- [ADR 0004](0004-orchestration-abstraction.md) — the unified `OrchestrationProvider` abstraction this webhook plugs into; `AdfProvider.parse_event` consumes the authenticated payload.
64	- [ADR 0007](0007-airflow-callback-model.md) — the Airflow sibling; uses HMAC-signed-header auth because Airflow callbacks (unlike Azure Monitor) can set custom headers. Rotation (hard cutover) and replay (idempotent-upsert only, no freshness check) decisions are shared between the two.
65	- Shared secret config (`ADF_WEBHOOK_SECRET`) and the receiver land in the Week 2 ADF webhook-receiver PR.
66	- A security review before the Week 7 deploy should re-examine secret-in-URL exposure.
67	
```

1	# ADR 0004 — Unified `OrchestrationProvider` abstraction for ADF and Apache Airflow
2	
3	- **Status:** Accepted
4	- **Date:** 2026-05-24
5	- **Deciders:** @TheurgicDuke771
6	
7	## Context
8	
9	DataQ integrates with Azure Data Factory (ADF) and Apache Airflow. The original product framing listed ADF as a "5th datasource type," which conflates orchestration with data storage:
10	
11	- **Datasources** (Snowflake, ADLS Gen2, S3, Unity Catalog) are stores against which DQ checks are written.
12	- **Orchestrators** (ADF, Airflow) are workflow engines whose pipeline/DAG runs we observe and react to. We do not write DQ checks against the orchestrator itself.
13	
14	Treating orchestrators as datasources pollutes the suite/check editor, mixes unrelated concerns in the data model, and makes the upcoming Airflow integration look like a one-off rather than a sibling of ADF.
15	
16	## Decision
17	
18	**Treat ADF and Apache Airflow as orchestration integrations behind a single `OrchestrationProvider` abstraction. They are NOT datasources and never appear in the connection editor / check editor / suite model as a queryable target.**
19	
20	### Responsibilities (identical across both providers)
21	
22	1. **Monitor** pipeline/DAG runs → stored in `pipeline_runs` table with a `provider` column (`adf` | `airflow`) and `provider_run_id`.
23	2. **Detect failure** in near-real-time via provider-specific webhook channels (see table below).
24	3. **Trigger suite execution on successful completion** via `trigger_bindings`. The table has a surrogate primary key (`id`) and a non-unique composite **lookup index** on (`provider`, `pipeline_or_dag_id`, `env`) — one pipeline/DAG can map to many suites (one row per binding). Failure events alert the user but do NOT trigger suite runs (no point running checks on data that wasn't loaded).
25	
26	### Interface
27	
28	```
29	class OrchestrationProvider:
30	    def parse_event(self, payload: bytes, headers: dict) -> RunUpdate: ...
31	    def fetch_run_detail(self, provider_run_id: str) -> RunDetail: ...
32	    def list_recent_runs(self, since: datetime) -> list[RunUpdate]: ...
33	```
34	
35	Both `AdfProvider` and `AirflowProvider` implement this interface. Service code routes by `provider` enum, never by provider-specific branching.
36	
37	### Event channels per provider
38	
39	| Provider | Failure / success channel | Auth | Polling fallback |
40	|---|---|---|---|
41	| ADF | Azure Monitor alert rule → webhook `POST /api/v1/orchestration/events/adf` | Shared-secret header (Azure Monitor's only auth mode) | ADF REST API every 10 min |
42	| Airflow | DAG `on_success_callback` / `on_failure_callback` → webhook `POST /api/v1/orchestration/events/airflow` | HMAC-signed payload (signing key in Key Vault) | Airflow REST API `dagRuns` every 10 min |
43	
44	### Single-orchestrator-per-`(provider, env)` assumption
45	
46	`trigger_bindings` is keyed by (`provider`, `pipeline_or_dag_id`, `env`) → `suite_id`. This composite key **cannot disambiguate two instances of the same provider in the same environment** — e.g. two separate `airflow` deployments both serving `env=dev`. The agreed v1 shape therefore assumes **exactly one orchestrator instance per (`provider`, `env`) pair**.
47	
48	**Consequence:** to keep the binding lookup unambiguous, one of two things must hold:
49	
50	1. Connection-level CRUD enforces **uniqueness on (`type`, `env`) for orchestrator-typed connections** (an `adf`/`airflow` connection is singular per env), OR
51	2. `trigger_bindings` grows a `connection_id` column so a binding names a specific orchestrator instance.
52	
53	**v1 decision:** take option 1 — document the assumption (this section) and **enforce `(type, env)` uniqueness at the connection-CRUD layer in Week 2** for orchestrator-typed connections. The schema bump (option 2) is **deferred to v1.1** and only revisited if multi-instance-per-env becomes a real requirement. Without this guard, a future contributor adding a second same-env Airflow connection would hit a silent binding collision rather than a validation error.
54	
55	### UI surface
56	
57	Orchestrators appear ONLY in:
58	- The orchestration status panel on the results dashboard.
59	- The trigger-binding configuration UI.
60	
61	They do NOT appear in the connection editor's "pick a datasource" list or the check editor's table picker.
62	
63	## Consequences
64	
65	**Positive**
66	- Adding a third orchestration provider in the future (Prefect, Dagster, etc.) is a new `OrchestrationProvider` implementation — no data-model or UI churn.
67	- `pipeline_runs` stays clean as a single events stream regardless of provider.
68	- `trigger_bindings` is provider-agnostic from day one.
69	- Forces correct mental model — orchestrator is not a datasource.
70	
71	**Negative**
72	- Slightly more abstraction upfront in Week 2 vs hardcoding ADF, then refactoring when Airflow is added. Accepted because Airflow is in-scope for v1, not a hypothetical future.
73	- Airflow callback adoption is voluntary on the user side (we cannot mutate their DAGs). Mitigated by documenting the polling fallback and providing a copy-paste `dataq_airflow_callback` snippet.
74	
75	## Alternatives considered
76	
77	- **Treat ADF as a 5th datasource (original framing)** — rejected. Conflates orchestration with storage; pollutes the check editor and the data model.
78	- **Hardcode ADF in v1, abstract later when Airflow is added** — rejected. Refactoring after `pipeline_runs` has data is more expensive than designing the abstraction once upfront.
79	
80	## Related
81	
82	- `pipeline_runs` and `trigger_bindings` schema lands in Week 1/2.
83	- `OrchestrationProvider` interface lands in Week 2 alongside both implementations.
84	- The single-orchestrator-per-`(provider, env)` assumption (above) was surfaced in [PR #41](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/pull/41) review and tracked in [#72](https://github.com/TheurgicDuke771/DataQ/issues/72); the `(type, env)` uniqueness guard is a Week 2 connection-CRUD requirement.
85	- Future: ADR 0006 (ADF webhook auth) and ADR 0007 (Airflow callback model) will detail the provider-specific event channels.
86	
```

17	
18	REQUEST_ID_HEADER: Final = "X-Request-ID"
19	# Validate caller-supplied X-Request-ID before echoing it (security audit
20	# 2026-05-28): cap length, restrict charset so log lines and response
21	# headers can't be polluted with arbitrary content.
22	_REQUEST_ID_RE: Final = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}$")
23	
24	_log = get_logger(__name__)
25	
26	
27	@asynccontextmanager
28	async def lifespan(_app: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
29	    configure_logging()
30	    logger = get_logger(__name__)
31	    settings = get_settings()
32	    logger.info(
33	        "app_startup",
34	        environment=settings.environment,
35	        log_level=settings.log_level,
36	        app_insights_enabled=bool(settings.applicationinsights_connection_string),
37	    )
38	    await init_auth()
39	    yield
40	    logger.info("app_shutdown")
41	
42	
43	app = FastAPI(title="DataQ API", lifespan=lifespan)

45	
46	@app.middleware("http")
47	async def request_id_middleware(
48	    request: Request, call_next: Callable[[Request], Awaitable[Response]]
49	) -> Response:
50	    incoming = request.headers.get(REQUEST_ID_HEADER)
51	    rid = incoming if incoming and _REQUEST_ID_RE.match(incoming) else uuid.uuid4().hex
52	    token = request_id_var.set(rid)
53	    start = time.perf_counter()
54	    try:
55	        response = await call_next(request)
56	    except Exception:
57	        elapsed_ms = round((time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000, 2)
58	        _log.exception(
59	            "request_failed",
60	            method=request.method,
61	            path=request.url.path,
62	            duration_ms=elapsed_ms,
63	        )
64	        request_id_var.reset(token)
65	        raise
66	    elapsed_ms = round((time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000, 2)
67	    _log.info(
68	        "request",
69	        method=request.method,
70	        path=request.url.path,
71	        status=response.status_code,
72	        duration_ms=elapsed_ms,
73	    )
74	    request_id_var.reset(token)
75	    response.headers[REQUEST_ID_HEADER] = rid
76	    return response
77

1	"""Idempotent seed for the Week 1 exit-gate probe.
2	
3	The probe endpoint runs a canned suite against a single seeded dev Snowflake
4	connection. Connection CRUD and suite/check authoring arrive in Weeks 2-3; until
5	then this get-or-creates the fixtures so the endpoint is safe to hit repeatedly.
6	
7	The canned check is column-agnostic (a row-count bound) so it works against any
8	configured table without assuming a schema.
9	"""
10	
11	from __future__ import annotations
12	
13	from typing import Any
14	
15	from sqlalchemy import select
16	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
17	
18	from backend.app.core.config import Settings
19	from backend.app.db.models import Check, Connection, Suite, User
20	
21	PROBE_CONNECTION_NAME = "probe-snowflake-dev"
22	PROBE_SUITE_NAME = "probe-snowflake-suite"
23	PROBE_ENV = "dev"
24	
25	# (name, expectation_type, config) — kept column-agnostic for now.
26	_PROBE_CHECKS: tuple[tuple[str, str, dict[str, Any]], ...] = (
27	    ("row_count_positive", "expect_table_row_count_to_be_between", {"min_value": 1}),
28	)
29	
30	
31	def _connection_config(settings: Settings) -> dict[str, Any]:
32	    return {
33	        "account": settings.probe_snowflake_account,
34	        "user": settings.probe_snowflake_user,
35	        "database": settings.probe_snowflake_database,
36	        "schema": settings.probe_snowflake_schema,
37	        "warehouse": settings.probe_snowflake_warehouse,
38	        "role": settings.probe_snowflake_role,
39	    }
40	
41	
42	def ensure_probe_fixtures(
43	    session: Session, *, user: User, settings: Settings
44	) -> tuple[Connection, Suite, list[Check]]:
45	    """Get-or-create the probe Connection, Suite, and Checks. Idempotent."""
46	    connection = session.scalars(
47	        select(Connection).where(
48	            Connection.name == PROBE_CONNECTION_NAME, Connection.env == PROBE_ENV
49	        )
50	    ).first()
51	    if connection is None:
52	        connection = Connection(
53	            name=PROBE_CONNECTION_NAME,
54	            type="snowflake",
55	            env=PROBE_ENV,
56	            config=_connection_config(settings),
57	            secret_ref=settings.probe_snowflake_secret_ref,
58	            created_by=user.id,
59	        )
60	        session.add(connection)
61	        session.flush()  # populate connection.id for the suite FK
62	
63	    suite = session.scalars(
64	        select(Suite).where(Suite.name == PROBE_SUITE_NAME, Suite.connection_id == connection.id)
65	    ).first()
66	    if suite is None:
67	        suite = Suite(
68	            name=PROBE_SUITE_NAME,
69	            description="Week 1 exit-gate probe suite",
70	            connection_id=connection.id,
71	            created_by=user.id,
72	        )
73	        session.add(suite)
74	        session.flush()  # populate suite.id for the check FK
75	
76	    checks = list(session.scalars(select(Check).where(Check.suite_id == suite.id)))
77	    existing_names = {c.name for c in checks}
78	    for name, expectation_type, config in _PROBE_CHECKS:
79	        if name not in existing_names:
80	            check = Check(
81	                suite_id=suite.id,
82	                name=name,
83	                expectation_type=expectation_type,
84	                config=dict(config),
85	            )
86	            session.add(check)
87	            checks.append(check)
88	
89	    session.commit()
90	    return connection, suite, checks
91
