null_fraction=(null_count / row_count) if row_count else 0.0,\n                distinct_count=int(non_null.nunique()),\n                min_value=sanitize_json(_to_native(non_null.min())) if path=path, file_format=file_format, row_count=row_count, columns=profiles\n    )\n\n\ndef _read_dataframe(\n    connection: Connection, *, path: str, file_format: str, secret_store: SecretStore\n) -> io.BytesIO(_download_bytes(connection, path, secret_store))\n    if file_format == \"csv\":\n        return pd.read_csv(raw, nrows=_SAMPLE_ROWS)\n    return pd.read_parquet(raw).head(_SAMPLE_ROWS)\n\n\ndef _download_bytes(connection: Connection, path: str, secret_store: SecretStore) -> bytes:\n    \"\"\"Fetch the object/blob bytes from S3 or ADLS Gen2 \"s3\",\n            region_name=cfg.region,\n            aws_access_key_id=cfg.access_key_id,\n            aws_secret_access_key=secret,\n            config=Config(connect_timeout=_LOGIN_TIMEOUT, read_timeout=_NETWORK_TIMEOUT),\n        )\n        body: bytes = client.get_object(Bucket=cfg.bucket, Key=path)[\"Body\"].read()\n        return body\n\n    from azure.storage.blob import BlobServiceClient\n\n    acfg = AdlsConfig.model_validate(connection.config)\n    client_az: Any = BlobServiceClient(account_url=acfg.account_url, credential=secret)\n    try:\n        blob = client_az.get_blob_client(container=acfg.container, blob=path)\n        downloaded: bytes = blob.download_blob().readall()\n        return downloaded\n    finally:\n        client_az.close()\n\n\ndef profile_file(\n    connection: Connection,\n    *,\n    path: str,\n    file_format: str | None,\n    columns: list[str],\n    top_n: int,\n    secret_store: SecretStore,\n) -> ProfileResult:\n    \"\"\"Profile `columns` of a flat file on `connection` (ADLS Gen2 / S3).\n\n    Raises `ProfileTargetInvalidError` (422) for an unknown format,\n    `ProfileColumnNotFoundError` (422) for a missing column, and\n    `ProfileFailedError` (502) if the file can't be read — the underlying\n    exception is never echoed (it can carry credential/endpoint fragments).\n    \"\"\"\n    fmt = infer_file_format(path, file_format)\n    try:\n        df = _read_dataframe(connection, path=path, file_format=fmt, secret_store=secret_store)\n    except Exception as exc:\n        log.warning(\n SecretStore,\n) -> ProfileResult:\n    \"\"\"Dispatch to the SQL or flat-file profiler based on the connection type.\n\n    Raises `ProfileUnsupportedError` (422) for a type with no profiler, and\n    `ProfileTargetInvalidError` (422) if the target for that type is missing\n    (a SQL type needs `table`; a flat-file type needs `path`).\n    \"\"\"\n    if connection.type in _SQL_TYPES:\n        if All green — 413 passed, mypy + bandit clean. The flat-file profiler works.

Now to your question — it's a good one, and the honest answer is **partially, with two gaps worth closing before this merges**:

**`enhancingperf.html` (Cython/Numba/`eval`/`query`)** — **not applicable here.** Those help when you have row-wise Python loops or complex expressions. Our stats are already pure vectorized pandas/C calls (`isna().sum()`, `nunique()`, `min/max`, `value_counts()`) — there's no Python-level loop over rows to accelerate. Reaching for Numba here would add a heavy dep for zero gain.

**`scale.html` ("load less data")** — **we use row sampling (`nrows`/`head`) but I missed the bigger win: column projection.** The code currently downloads the file and reads **all** columns, then profiles the 1–3 the user asked for. Profiling 3 of 200 columns shouldn't read 200. Let me fix that now (it's cheap and clearly correct) before committing:

Reads at most\n    `_SAMPLE_ROWS` rows; for CSV the cap is pushed into the parser, for Parquet\n    the frame is sliced after load.\n    \"\"\"\n    import pandas as pd\n\n    raw = io.BytesIO(_download_bytes(connection, path, secret_store))\n    if file_format == \"csv\":\n        return pd.read_csv(raw, nrows=_SAMPLE_ROWS)\n    return pd.read_parquet(raw).head(_SAMPLE_ROWS)",
  "new_string": "    connection: Connection,\n    *,\n    path: str,\n    file_format: str,\n    columns: list[str],\n    secret_store: SecretStore,\n) -> Any:\n    \"\"\"Download `path` from the flat-file datasource into a sampled dataframe.\n\n    The live I/O seam (download + parse) — monkeypatched in tests. Applies the two\n    \"load less data\" levers from the pandas scaling guide:\n\n    * **column projection** — only the requested `columns` are parsed (CSV\n      `usecols`, Parquet `columns=`), so profiling 3 of 200 columns doesn't read\n      all 200. Unknown names are simply not selected; `profile_dataframe` then\n      reports genuinely-missing ones as a clean 422.\n    * **row sampling** — at most `_SAMPLE_ROWS` rows (CSV pushes the cap into the\n      parser; Parquet is sliced after the projected read).\n\n    Not done (deliberate, for an authoring-time sampler): streaming/range reads —\n    the whole object is still downloaded before parsing — and out-of-core engines\n    (Dask). Both are future work if a profiling-cost problem actually shows up.\n    \"\"\"\n    import pandas as pd\n\n    wanted = set(columns)\n    raw = io.BytesIO(_download_bytes(connection, path, secret_store))\n    if file_format == \"csv\":\n        return pd.read_csv(raw, nrows=_SAMPLE_ROWS, usecols=lambda name: name in wanted)\n\n    import pyarrow.parquet as pq\n\n    available = set(pq.ParquetFile(raw).schema.names)\n    raw.seek(0)\n    present = [c for c in columns if c in available]\n    return pd.read_parquet(raw, columns=present).head(_SAMPLE_ROWS)"
}

  "new_string": "    import pyarrow.parquet as pq\n\n    # pyarrow ships only partial types; ParquetFile is an untyped call.\n    available = set(pq.ParquetFile(raw).schema.names)  # type: ignore[no-untyped-call]\n    raw.seek(0)"

> AGENT

`strict = true` turns on both `warn_unused_ignores` **and** `warn_redundant_casts`, so any `# type: ignore` or `cast(Any, …)` flips between needed/unused depending on whether pyarrow is installed — neither works across both envs. The robust fix is to force pyarrow to `Any` in **both** envs via `follow_imports = "skip"`, then drop the ignore entirely. ## Flat-file profiler — done ✅

PR #139 is merged. The column profiler now covers **Snowflake + ADLS Gen2 + S3** (2/3). One CI detour worth noting: the `type check` job exposed a real cross-environment fragility — pyarrow is installed on my machine but not in CI's slim typecheck deps, and `strict = true` made any `# type: ignore`/`cast` env-dependent. The durable fix (`follow_imports = "skip"`) makes the type-check deterministic regardless of whether pyarrow is installed — better than papering over it per-line.

And to close the loop on your pandas question: column projection (`usecols`/`columns=`) + row sampling are now in and test-verified; Cython/Numba weren't applicable (already vectorized); streaming/out-of-core are documented as deliberate deferrals.

> AGENT

Good probing — and the answer is more interesting once you check it against our *specific* code (a sampling, read-only profiler), so I verified each against our actual operations rather than guessing. Honest audit:

## Copy-on-Write — not enabled, and shouldn't be (here)
CoW's wins are about *mutation*: avoiding defensive copies on slice-then-assign and killing `SettingWithCopyWarning`. Our `profile_dataframe` is strictly read-only — `isna().sum()`, `dropna()`, `nunique()`, `min/max`, `value_counts()`; no in-place writes, no chained assignment. So CoW is ~a no-op for us. And it's a **process-global** flag (`pd.options.mode.copy_on_write`) that would also change GX's heavy pandas usage — so flipping it for the profiler would be inappropriate. It's a real *pandas-3.0-readiness* decision, but an app-wide one, separate from this feature.

## Zero-copy Arrow-backed dtypes — not used; the one with real (if bounded) merit
This applies to the **Parquet** path: parquet is already Arrow and we already depend on pyarrow, so `read_parquet(..., dtype_backend="pyarrow")` is a genuine zero-copy + faster-strings win. I checked the compatibility risk — and it's **fine**: with Arrow dtypes, `min()`→Python `int`, `max()` on timestamps→`pd.Timestamp`, `value_counts` keys→`str`, so our `_to_native` coercion still works (it just doesn't take the numpy `.item()` branch). The one thing needing tests is `pd.NA` vs numpy `NaN` null semantics. **Caveat:** the payoff is bounded because we already sample (`_SAMPLE_ROWS`) and project columns, so the frame is small by construction.

## pyarrow CSV engine — verified *counterproductive* for us
`read_csv(engine="pyarrow")` is multithreaded/faster, but I confirmed it **rejects both scale levers we just added**:
```
nrows  -> ValueError: 'nrows' is not supported with the 'pyarrow' engine
usecols(callable) -> ValueError: pyarrow engine does not allow 'usecols' to be a callable
```
So adopting it would force us to drop row-cap-at-parse and flexible projection — a net loss. Not worth it.

## Bottom line
The only one worth adopting is **Arrow-backed dtypes on the Parquet branch**, and it's a marginal, low-risk improvement given we already sample + project. CoW and the pyarrow CSV engine are correctly *not* used.

1	"""Unity Catalog (Databricks) connection adapter.
2	
3	A datasource (CLAUDE.md §4): DQ checks run against Unity Catalog tables via a
4	Databricks SQL Warehouse. Week 2 ships only the `ConnectionAdapter` seam (config
5	validation + connectivity `test`).
6	
7	**Runner seam note:** the *check-run* path for UC must sit behind a
8	``UnityCatalogCheckRunner`` interface so v1.1 can swap GX for Databricks Labs DQX
9	on DLT/streaming (CLAUDE.md §5, ADR 0003). That runner is Week-3 work and is
10	deliberately **not** built here — this module is connection config + a
11	connectivity probe only.
12	
13	Auth is a **personal access token (PAT)** — the v1 default, held in the
14	SecretStore (no credential-less mode, so none of the ADLS/S3 ``secret_ref``
15	nullability deferral applies). ``test`` opens a SQL-Warehouse connection and runs
16	``SELECT 1`` — a green test means the workspace + warehouse are reachable and the
17	PAT authenticates. ``databricks-sql-connector`` is imported lazily (per
18	``core/secrets.py``); like the other adapters it runs live and fails-soft pending
19	real credentials.
20	"""
21	
22	from __future__ import annotations
23	
24	from typing import Any
25	from urllib.parse import urlparse
26	
27	from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, field_validator
28	
29	
30	class UnityCatalogConfig(BaseModel):
31	    """Non-secret Databricks/UC connection config (the PAT comes from secrets).
32	
33	    Maps from ``Connection.config``. ``workspace_url`` is the workspace root
34	    (e.g. ``https://adb-1234.5.azuredatabricks.net``); ``warehouse_id`` is the
35	    SQL Warehouse id, from which the connector's ``http_path`` is built. The PAT
36	    is resolved from the SecretStore at test time.
37	    """
38	
39	    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")
40	
41	    workspace_url: str
42	    warehouse_id: str
43	
44	    @field_validator("workspace_url")
45	    @classmethod
46	    def _http_url(cls, value: str) -> str:
47	        if not value.startswith(("http://", "https://")):
48	            raise ValueError("workspace_url must start with http:// or https://")
49	        return value.rstrip("/")
50	
51	    @property
52	    def server_hostname(self) -> str:
53	        return urlparse(self.workspace_url).netloc
54	
55	    @property
56	    def http_path(self) -> str:
57	        return f"/sql/1.0/warehouses/{self.warehouse_id}"
58	
59	
60	class UnityCatalogConnectionAdapter:
61	    """`ConnectionAdapter` for Unity Catalog — config validation + a SELECT 1 probe."""
62	
63	    def validate_config(self, raw: dict[str, Any]) -> UnityCatalogConfig:
64	        return UnityCatalogConfig.model_validate(raw)
65	
66	    def test(self, raw: dict[str, Any], secret: str) -> None:
67	        """Open a SQL-Warehouse connection and run ``SELECT 1``; raise on failure.
68	
69	        ``secret`` is the Databricks PAT. Deliberately GX/DQX-free — a lightweight
70	        connectivity probe, not a suite run.
71	        """
72	        from databricks import sql
73	
74	        config = self.validate_config(raw)
75	        # databricks-sql-connector is only partially typed; treat the connection
76	        # as dynamic so strict mypy doesn't flag no-untyped-call on its methods.
77	        connection: Any = sql.connect(
78	            server_hostname=config.server_hostname,
79	            http_path=config.http_path,
80	            access_token=secret,
81	        )
82	        try:
83	            cursor = connection.cursor()
84	            try:
85	                cursor.execute("SELECT 1")
86	                cursor.fetchone()
87	            finally:
88	                cursor.close()
89	        finally:
90	            connection.close()
91

198	    *,
199	    table: str,
200	    schema: str,

202	    aggregate: Mapping[str, Any],
203	    top_values: dict[str, list[Mapping[str, Any]]],

234	def _open_connection(connection: Connection, secret_store: SecretStore) -> Generator[Any]:
235	    """Yield a live SQLAlchemy connection to the datasource, disposing the engine."""
236	    from sqlalchemy import create_engine
237	
238	    if not connection.secret_ref:

244	        connect_args={"login_timeout": _LOGIN_TIMEOUT, "network_timeout": _NETWORK_TIMEOUT},
245	    )
246	    try:
247	        with engine.connect() as conn:
248	            yield conn
249	    finally:

  "old_string": "@contextmanager\ndef _open_connection(connection: Connection, secret_store: SecretStore) -> Generator[Any]:\n    \"\"\"Yield a live SQLAlchemy connection to the datasource, disposing the engine.\"\"\"\n    from sqlalchemy import create_engine\n\n    if not connection.secret_ref:\n        raise ValueError(\"connection requires secret_ref for the password\")\n    config = SnowflakeConfig.model_validate(connection.config)\n    password = secret_store.get(connection.secret_ref)\n    engine = create_engine(\n        build_connection_string(config, password),\n        connect_args={\"login_timeout\": _LOGIN_TIMEOUT, \"network_timeout\": _NETWORK_TIMEOUT},\n    )\n    try:\n        with engine.connect() as conn:\n            yield conn\n    finally:\n        engine.dispose()",
  "new_string": "def _engine_args(connection: Connection, secret: str) -> tuple[str, dict[str, Any]]:\n    \"\"\"Build the (SQLAlchemy URL, connect_args) for a SQL datasource connection.\"\"\"\n    if connection.type == \"unity_catalog\":\n        cfg = UnityCatalogConfig.model_validate(connection.config)\n        # Catalog is not pinned on the URL — the query qualifies catalog.schema.table.\n        url = (\n            f\"REDACTED\"\n            f\"?http_path={quote_plus(cfg.http_path)}\"\n        )\n        return url, {}\n    sf = SnowflakeConfig.model_validate(connection.config)\n    return build_connection_string(sf, secret), {\n        \"login_timeout\": _LOGIN_TIMEOUT,\n        \"network_timeout\": _NETWORK_TIMEOUT,\n    }\n\n\n@contextmanager\ndef _open_connection(connection: Connection, secret_store: SecretStore) -> Generator[Any]:\n    \"\"\"Yield a live SQLAlchemy connection to the datasource, disposing the engine.\"\"\"\n    from sqlalchemy import create_engine\n\n    if not connection.secret_ref:\n        raise ValueError(\"connection requires secret_ref for the credential\")\n    secret = secret_store.get(connection.secret_ref)\n    url, connect_args = _engine_args(connection, secret)\n    engine = create_engine(url, connect_args=connect_args)\n    try:\n        with engine.connect() as conn:\n            yield conn\n    finally:\n        engine.dispose()"
}

495	    Raises `ProfileTargetInvalidError` (422) for an unknown format,
496	    `ProfileColumnNotFoundError` (422) for a missing column, and
497	    `ProfileFailedError` (502) if the file can't be read — the underlying
498	    exception is never echoed (it can carry credential/endpoint fragments).
499	    """
500	    fmt = infer_file_format(path, file_format)
501	    try:
502	        df = _read_dataframe(
503	            connection, path=path, file_format=fmt, columns=columns, secret_store=secret_store
504	        )
505	    except Exception as exc:
506	        log.warning(
507	            "column_profile_failed", connection_type=connection.type, error_type=type(exc).__name__
508	        )
509	        raise ProfileFailedError(
510	            "column profile could not read the file", detail={"path": path}
511	        ) from exc
512	
513	    return profile_dataframe(df, columns=columns, top_n=top_n, path=path, file_format=fmt)
514	
515	
516	def profile_connection(
517	    connection: Connection,

## Design highlights

- **Maximal reuse, minimal new code** — UC joins the existing SQL branch and reuses `profile_table` + the Core query builders + `assemble_profile`. The only genuinely new pieces are the engine dispatch (`_engine_args` → Databricks SQLAlchemy URL) and the 3-level namespace.
- **The one real subtlety** — Unity Catalog's `catalog.schema.table`. I verified offline (compiling against the real Databricks dialect) that a dotted *schema* gets quoted as a single identifier (wrong), so I used `quoted_name(..., quote=False)` to emit three proper dotted parts. Still allowlist-validated and still Core expression language — no raw SQL.
- 12 new tests; full suite 425 passed; `profile_service` 86% (only the live network seams uncovered).

1	"""Datasource adapter seam.
2	
3	Every datasource (Snowflake now; ADLS / S3 / Unity Catalog later) executes DQ
4	checks behind one ``CheckRunner`` interface that speaks GX-agnostic DTOs. The
5	GX-specific machinery lives entirely inside each adapter, so the run-service and
6	its tests depend only on the types here — never on Great Expectations internals.
7	This is also the seam that lets v1.1 swap GX for DQX on Unity Catalog (CLAUDE.md
8	§5) without rippling into the suite / check / result layer.
9	
10	`CheckSpec` goes in (a check pulled from the DB); `CheckOutcome` comes out, one
11	per check, shaped to map cleanly onto the `results` table columns. Adapters
12	translate GX results into these DTOs; tests provide a fake `CheckRunner` and
13	never touch a live datasource.
14	"""
15	
16	from __future__ import annotations
17	
18	from dataclasses import dataclass
19	from typing import Any, Protocol, runtime_checkable
20	
21	from pydantic import BaseModel
22	
23	
24	@dataclass(frozen=True)
25	class CheckSpec:
26	    """One expectation to evaluate, sourced from a `checks` row.
27	
28	    `expectation_type` is the GX snake_case name (e.g.
29	    ``expect_column_values_to_not_be_null``); `kwargs` are its parameters
30	    (e.g. ``{"column": "id"}``). Adapters own the translation to the concrete
31	    GX expectation class.
32	    """
33	
34	    expectation_type: str
35	    kwargs: dict[str, Any]
36	
37	
38	@dataclass(frozen=True)
39	class CheckOutcome:
40	    """Result of one check, shaped for the `results` table.
41	
42	    `observed_value` / `expected_value` / `sample_failures` land in the
43	    matching JSONB columns. `sample_failures` may contain real data rows, so it
44	    is governed by the retention sweep and must only ever be logged through the
45	    PII-redacting structlog chain.
46	    """
47	
48	    expectation_type: str
49	    success: bool
50	    observed_value: dict[str, Any] | None = None
51	    expected_value: dict[str, Any] | None = None
52	    sample_failures: dict[str, Any] | None = None
53	
54	
55	@dataclass(frozen=True)
56	class SuiteOutcome:
57	    """Aggregate result of running a list of checks against one table."""
58	
59	    success: bool
60	    checks: list[CheckOutcome]
61	
62	
63	@runtime_checkable
64	class CheckRunner(Protocol):
65	    """Executes a set of checks against a single table and returns outcomes."""
66	
67	    def run_checks(
68	        self,
69	        *,
70	        table: str,
71	        schema: str | None,
72	        checks: list[CheckSpec],
73	    ) -> SuiteOutcome: ...
74	
75	
76	@runtime_checkable
77	class ConnectionAdapter(Protocol):
78	    """Per-datasource-type connection behaviour: config validation + live test.
79	
80	    The two things that vary across connection types (Snowflake now; ADF, ADLS,
81	    S3, Unity Catalog next) behind one interface, so connection-CRUD service code
82	    dispatches by ``connection.type`` and never branches on it. Each adapter owns
83	    its own pydantic config model; both methods take the raw config dict so the
84	    adapter is the single source of truth for that type's shape.
85	
86	    `validate_config` parses + validates a stored/incoming config (raising
87	    pydantic ``ValidationError`` on bad input) and returns the normalised model.
88	    `test` resolves connectivity against the live datasource using the config +
89	    its secret, raising on failure. Adapters never touch the DB or SecretStore —
90	    the caller resolves the secret and hands it in.
91	    """
92	
93	    def validate_config(self, raw: dict[str, Any]) -> BaseModel: ...
94	
95	    def test(self, raw: dict[str, Any], secret: str) -> None: ...
96

1	"""Execute a suite's checks via a datasource adapter and persist the results.
2	
3	This is the GX-agnostic core of a run: it drives the `Run` lifecycle, calls a
4	`CheckRunner` (injected — Snowflake in production, a fake in tests), and maps the
5	returned `SuiteOutcome` onto `Result` rows. GX/Snowflake specifics live behind
6	the adapter; this layer only knows the DTOs in ``datasources.base``.
7	
8	Run.status describes *execution*, not data quality: a run that completes is
9	``succeeded`` even when checks fail (the failures live in ``Result.status`` /
10	``SuiteOutcome.success``). ``failed`` means the run could not execute — the
11	adapter raised (e.g. could not reach the warehouse).
12	"""
13	
14	from __future__ import annotations
15	
16	import uuid
17	from datetime import UTC, datetime
18	
19	from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
20	
21	from backend.app.core.jsonsafe import sanitize_json
22	from backend.app.core.logging import get_logger
23	from backend.app.datasources.base import CheckOutcome, CheckRunner, CheckSpec
24	from backend.app.db.models import Check, Result, Run
25	from backend.app.services.severity import derive_status, extract_metric
26	
27	log = get_logger(__name__)
28	
29	
30	def _now() -> datetime:
31	    return datetime.now(UTC)
32	
33	
34	def _build_result(run_id: uuid.UUID, check: Check, outcome: CheckOutcome) -> Result:
35	    """Map a check + its GX outcome to a `Result`, deriving the severity tier.
36	
37	    The unexpected-percent badness scalar is extracted once and used both to band
38	    the tier (ADR 0005 / 0016) and to persist as the durable, SQL-aggregatable
39	    `metric_value` (ADR 0012). `duration_ms` stays NULL in v1 — per-check timing
40	    isn't separable from GX's single suite-level `validate()` (reserved seam).
41	    """
42	    metric = extract_metric(outcome)
43	    status = derive_status(
44	        success=outcome.success,
45	        metric_value=metric,
46	        warn_threshold=check.warn_threshold,
47	        fail_threshold=check.fail_threshold,
48	        critical_threshold=check.critical_threshold,
49	    )
50	    return Result(
51	        run_id=run_id,
52	        check_id=check.id,
53	        status=status,
54	        metric_value=metric,
55	        observed_value=sanitize_json(outcome.observed_value),
56	        expected_value=sanitize_json(outcome.expected_value),
57	        sample_failures=sanitize_json(outcome.sample_failures),
58	    )
59	
60	
61	_EXPECTATION_KIND = "expectation"
62	
63	
64	def _specs_for_checks(checks: list[Check]) -> list[CheckSpec]:
65	    """Dispatch checks by `check.kind` to their runner input (ADR 0012).
66	
67	    v1 implements only the `expectation` kind (the GX `CheckRunner`). The other
68	    reserved kinds (`freshness`/`volume`/`schema_drift`/`anomaly`/`comparison`)
69	    are constraint-valid but have no runner yet, so a run containing one raises
70	    `NotImplementedError` rather than silently feeding it to GX as an
71	    expectation. This dispatch composes with the connection-type `CheckRunner`
72	    selection (Week 5, ADR 0011): `kind` chooses the *monitor*, `connection.type`
73	    chooses the *adapter*.
74	    """
75	    unsupported = sorted({c.kind for c in checks if c.kind != _EXPECTATION_KIND})
76	    if unsupported:
77	        raise NotImplementedError(
78	            f"no run path for check kind(s) {', '.join(unsupported)}; "
79	            f"only {_EXPECTATION_KIND!r} is implemented in v1"
80	        )
81	    return [CheckSpec(expectation_type=c.expectation_type, kwargs=dict(c.config)) for c in checks]
82	
83	
84	def execute_run(
85	    session: Session,
86	    *,
87	    run: Run,
88	    checks: list[Check],
89	    runner: CheckRunner,
90	    table: str,
91	    schema: str | None = None,
92	) -> Run:
93	    """Run ``checks`` against ``table`` via ``runner`` and persist the outcome.
94	
95	    ``run`` must already be persisted (it carries the id the results link to).
96	    Returns the same `Run`, updated to ``succeeded`` or ``failed``.
97	    """
98	    run.status = "running"
99	    run.started_at = _now()
100	    session.commit()
101	    log.info(
102	        "run_started",
103	        run_id=str(run.id),
104	        suite_id=str(run.suite_id),
105	        n_checks=len(checks),
106	        table=table,
107	    )
108	
109	    # Everything from here — dispatching by kind, running the adapter, building
110	    # rows, and persisting them — is guarded so any failure drives the run to a
111	    # terminal 'failed' state. Without this, a DB error during add_all/commit (or
112	    # an unrunnable check kind) would leave the run stuck in 'running' forever.
113	    # rollback() discards any partial result inserts before we record the failure.
114	    try:
115	        specs = _specs_for_checks(checks)
116	        outcome = runner.run_checks(table=table, schema=schema, checks=specs)
117	        rows = [
118	            _build_result(run.id, check, check_outcome)
119	            for check, check_outcome in zip(checks, outcome.checks, strict=True)
120	        ]
121	        session.add_all(rows)
122	        run.status = "succeeded"
123	        run.finished_at = _now()
124	        session.commit()
125	    except Exception:
126	        session.rollback()
127	        run.status = "failed"
128	        run.finished_at = _now()
129	        session.commit()
130	        log.exception("run_failed", run_id=str(run.id), table=table)
131	        return run
132	
133	    log.info(
134	        "run_completed",
135	        run_id=str(run.id),
136	        suite_success=outcome.success,
137	        n_results=len(rows),
138	    )
139	    return run
140	
```

It lives here so every runner (Snowflake table,\nflat-file DataFrame, Unity Catalog later) reuses one implementation and the GX v1\nAPI is pinned in a single place (CLAUDE.md §5 — GX has drifted across releases).\n\nEach runner only differs in how it builds the GX *batch* (a Snowflake table\nasset vs an in-memory pandas asset); once it has a `batch_definition` it calls\n`run_expectations`, which registers the suite + validation definition and maps\nthe result. Tests exercise these pure parts with constructed GX results and a\ncanned DataFrame — no live datasource required.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom typing import Any\n\nimport \"unexpected_percent\")\n\n# GX injects internal bookkeeping keys into expectation_config.kwargs at run time\n# (e.g. batch_id); strip them so expected_value persists only the check's own\n# parameters.\n_GX_INTERNAL_KWARGS = frozenset({\"batch_id\"})\n\n\nclass UnknownExpectationError(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"Raised when a check's expectation_type has no matching GX expectation.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef _expectation_class_name(expectation_type: str) -> str:\n    \"\"\"snake_case GX type → PascalCase class name.\n\n    ``expect_column_values_to_not_be_null`` → ``ExpectColumnValuesToNotBeNull``.\n    \"\"\"\n    return \"\".join(part.title() for part in expectation_type.split(\"_\"))\n\n\ndef _to_gx_expectation(spec: CheckSpec) -> Any:\n    class_name = _expectation_class_name(spec.expectation_type)\n    expectation_cls = getattr(gxe, class_name, None)\n    if expectation_cls is None:\n        raise UnknownExpectationError(\n            f\"Unknown expectation_type {spec.expectation_type!r} (no gx class {class_name!r})\"\n        )\n    return expectation_cls(**spec.kwargs)\n\n\ndef _extract_sample_failures(result: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any] | None:\n    sample = {key: result[key] for key in _SAMPLE_KEYS if key in result}\n    return sample or None\n\n\ndef _expected_value(kwargs: Any) -> dict[str, Any] | None:\n    cleaned = {key: value for key, value in dict(kwargs).items() if key not in _GX_INTERNAL_KWARGS}\n    return cleaned or None\n\n\ndef to_suite_outcome(gx_result: Any) -> SuiteOutcome:\n    \"\"\"Map a GX ExpectationSuiteValidationResult onto our GX-agnostic DTO.\n\n    Kept GX-translation-only (no datasource specifics) so it is unit-testable\n    with a constructed GX result, no live datasource required.\n    \"\"\"\n    outcomes: list[CheckOutcome] = []\n    for check_result in gx_result.results:\n        config = check_result.expectation_config\n        detail: dict[str, Any] = check_result.result or {}\n        observed = (\n            {\"observed_value\": detail[\"observed_value\"]} if \"observed_value\" in detail else None\n        )\n        outcomes.append(\n            CheckOutcome(\n                expectation_type=config.type,\n                success=bool(check_result.success),\n                observed_value=observed,\n                expected_value=_expected_value(config.kwargs) if config.kwargs else None,\n                sample_failures=_extract_sample_failures(detail),\n            )\n        )\n    return SuiteOutcome(success=bool(gx_result.success), checks=outcomes)\n\n\ndef run_expectations(\n    context: Any,\n    *,\n    batch_definition: Any,\n    checks: list[CheckSpec],\n    name: str,\n    batch_parameters: dict[str, Any] | None = None,\n) -> SuiteOutcome:\n    \"\"\"Register the suite + validation definition for `batch_definition` and run.\n\n    The shared tail of every runner: GX 1.x requires the suite and validation\n    definition to be registered on the (ephemeral, per-run) context before\n    ``run()``. `batch_parameters` carries the in-memory DataFrame for a pandas\n    asset; it's empty for an asset that resolves its own batch (a SQL table).\n    \"\"\"\n    suite = context.suites.add(\n        gx.ExpectationSuite(\n            name=name,\n            expectations=[_to_gx_expectation(check) for check in checks],\n        )\n    )\n    validation_definition = context.validation_definitions.add(\n        gx.ValidationDefinition(name=f\"vd-{name}\", data=batch_definition, suite=suite)\n    )\n    result = validation_definition.run(\n        batch_parameters=batch_parameters or {}, result_format=\"COMPLETE\"\n    )\n    return to_suite_outcome(result)\n"
}

109	def to_suite_outcome(gx_result: Any) -> SuiteOutcome:
110	    """Map a GX ExpectationSuiteValidationResult onto our GX-agnostic DTO.
111	
112	    Kept module-level (not a private method) so it is unit-testable with a
113	    constructed GX result, no Snowflake connection required.
114	    """
115	    outcomes: list[CheckOutcome] = []
116	    for check_result in gx_result.results:
117	        config = check_result.expectation_config
118	        detail: dict[str, Any] = check_result.result or {}
119	        observed = (
120	            {"observed_value": detail["observed_value"]} if "observed_value" in detail else None
121	        )
122	        outcomes.append(
123	            CheckOutcome(
124	                expectation_type=config.type,
125	                success=bool(check_result.success),
126	                observed_value=observed,
127	                expected_value=_expected_value(config.kwargs) if config.kwargs else None,
128	                sample_failures=_extract_sample_failures(detail),
129	            )
130	        )
131	    return SuiteOutcome(success=bool(gx_result.success), checks=outcomes)

138	        self._config = config
139	        self._connection_string = build_connection_string(config, password)

142	        self,
143	        *,
144	        table: str,
145	        schema: str | None,
146	        checks: list[CheckSpec],
147	    ) -> SuiteOutcome:
148	        context = gx.get_context(mode="ephemeral")
149	        datasource = context.data_sources.add_snowflake(
150	            name=f"sf-{table}",
151	            connection_string=self._connection_string,
152	        )
153	        asset = datasource.add_table_asset(
154	            name=table,
155	            table_name=table,
156	            schema_name=schema or self._config.schema_,
157	        )
158	        batch_definition = asset.add_batch_definition_whole_table(name="whole_table")
159	        # GX 1.17 requires the suite and validation definition to be registered
160	        # on the context before run(); a free-standing ValidationDefinition.run()
161	        # raises ValidationDefinitionRelatedResourcesFreshnessError. The context
162	        # is ephemeral (per-run), so the fixed names never collide across runs.
163	        suite = context.suites.add(
164	            gx.ExpectationSuite(
165	                name=f"suite-{table}",
166	                expectations=[_to_gx_expectation(check) for check in checks],
167	            )
168	        )
169	        validation_definition = context.validation_definitions.add(
170	            gx.ValidationDefinition(
171	                name=f"vd-{table}",
172	                data=batch_definition,
173	                suite=suite,
174	            )
175	        )
176	        result = validation_definition.run(result_format="COMPLETE")
177	        return to_suite_outcome(result)

408	def _read_dataframe(
409	    connection: Connection,
410	    *,
411	    path: str,
412	    file_format: str,
413	    columns: list[str],
414	    secret_store: SecretStore,
415	) -> Any:
416	    """Download `path` from the flat-file datasource into a sampled dataframe.
417	
418	    The live I/O seam (download + parse) — monkeypatched in tests. Applies the two
419	    "load less data" levers from the pandas scaling guide:
420	
421	    * **column projection** — only the requested `columns` are parsed (CSV
422	      `usecols`, Parquet `columns=`), so profiling 3 of 200 columns doesn't read
423	      all 200. Unknown names are simply not selected; `profile_dataframe` then
424	      reports genuinely-missing ones as a clean 422.
425	    * **row sampling** — at most `_SAMPLE_ROWS` rows (CSV pushes the cap into the
426	      parser; Parquet is sliced after the projected read).
427	
428	    Not done (deliberate, for an authoring-time sampler): streaming/range reads —
429	    the whole object is still downloaded before parsing — and out-of-core engines
430	    (Dask). Both are future work if a profiling-cost problem actually shows up.
431	    """
432	    import pandas as pd
433	
434	    wanted = set(columns)
435	    raw = io.BytesIO(_download_bytes(connection, path, secret_store))
436	    if file_format == "csv":
437	        return pd.read_csv(raw, nrows=_SAMPLE_ROWS, usecols=lambda name: name in wanted)
438	
439	    import pyarrow.parquet as pq
440	
441	    available = set(pq.ParquetFile(raw).schema.names)
442	    raw.seek(0)
443	    present = [c for c in columns if c in available]
444	    # Parquet is already Arrow on disk; dtype_backend="pyarrow" keeps the buffers
445	    # zero-copy instead of materialising a numpy copy. The stat helpers + the
446	    # _to_native coercion are Arrow-scalar-safe (min/max → Python int/str,
447	    # timestamps → Timestamp.isoformat, NA dropped before reductions).
448	    return pd.read_parquet(raw, columns=present, dtype_backend="pyarrow").head(_SAMPLE_ROWS)

## Summary

`FlatFileCheckRunner` loads a file (S3/ADLS) into pandas and runs the suite's GX expectations against GX's DataFrame asset — so schema/row-count/null/value checks now run against flat files.

**Two clean refactors enabled it (no duplication):**
- **`gx_runner.py`** — extracted the GX translation + `run_expectations` flow that was Snowflake-specific; now shared by both runners (and the future UC runner). Snowflake re-exports the symbols so nothing downstream broke (its 21 tests still pass).
- **`flatfile.py`** — flat-file IO behind primitives (not the ORM, matching `build_snowflake_runner`); the column profiler now shares it instead of its own copy.

**Testability win:** GX runs in-process on the DataFrame, so I tested the *real* GX execution with a canned frame (asserting per-check pass/fail + `observed_value`) — only the network download is the deferred seam. `gx_runner` 100%, full suite 439 passed.

**Deliberately deferred** (flagged in the PR): connection-type→runner dispatch (Week-5 wiring), freshness-by-filename (reserved `freshness` kind, ADR 0012), and batch resolution (the sibling flat-file task).

I'll merge once CI is green and report back. After this, the remaining Week-3 tasks are **batch resolution** and the **UC check path + cross-datasource integration tests**.

GX's `add_databricks_sql` is pushdown, but the roadmap (and the DQX seam) calls for a **DataFrame** path. I'll mirror the flat-file runner: SELECT the table via the Databricks SQLAlchemy engine into pandas, then run GX on the DataFrame — fully testable (unlike pushdown, which needs a live warehouse).   "new_string": "        try:\n            cursor = connection.cursor()\n            try:\n                cursor.execute(\"SELECT 1\")\n                cursor.fetchone()\n            finally:\n                cursor.close()\n        finally:\n            connection.close()\n\n\ndef build_databricks_url(\n    config: UnityCatalogConfig, token: str, *, catalog: str | None = None\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"SQLAlchemy URL for the Databricks SQL Warehouse (databricks dialect).\n\n    The PAT, http_path and `catalog` are URL-encoded. Pinning `catalog` sets the\n    session default so a 2-level `schema.table` reference resolves to\n    `catalog.schema.table`; the profiler leaves it unset and qualifies the\n    namespace in the query instead.\n    \"\"\"\n    url = (\n        f\"REDACTED\"\n        f\"?http_path={quote_plus(config.http_path)}\"\n    )\n    if catalog:\n        url += f\"&catalog={quote_plus(catalog)}\"\n    return url\n\n\nclass UnityCatalogCheckRunner:\n    \"\"\"GX `CheckRunner` for Unity Catalog via the Databricks SQL Warehouse.\n\n    The UC run path reads the target table into a pandas DataFrame and validates\n    that frame with GX — the \"GX DataFrame datasource\" shape (CLAUDE.md §5), the\n    same shape Databricks Labs DQX consumes, so v1.1 can swap GX for DQX behind\n    this same interface without touching the suite/check/result layer.\n\n    `table` + `schema` come from `run_checks` (the suite's target); `catalog` is\n    fixed per run (held here). Reflecting + reading the table is the live seam\n    (`_read_table`), monkeypatched in tests; GX then runs in-process on the\n    returned frame, so the validation path itself is fully covered.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, *, config: UnityCatalogConfig, token: str, catalog: str) -> None:\n        self._config = config\n        self._token = token\n        self._catalog = catalog\n\n    def _read_table(self, *, table: str, schema: str | None) -> Any:\n        \"\"\"Reflect + read the whole table into a DataFrame (live seam).\n\n        `read_sql_table` reflects through SQLAlchemy (proper dialect quoting), so\n        the table/schema identifiers are never string-formatted into SQL; the\n        pinned catalog + `schema` qualify it to `catalog.schema.table`.\n        \"\"\"\n        import pandas as pd\n        from sqlalchemy import create_engine\n\n        engine = create_engine(build_databricks_url(self._config, self._token, catalog=self._catalog))\n        try:\n            return pd.read_sql_table(table, engine, schema=schema)\n        finally:\n            engine.dispose()\n\n    def run_checks(\n        self, *, table: str, schema: str | None, checks: list[CheckSpec]\n    ) -> SuiteOutcome:\n        df = self._read_table(table=table, schema=schema)\n        context = gx.get_context(mode=\"ephemeral\")\n        asset = context.data_sources.add_pandas(name=\"uc\").add_dataframe_asset(name=\"table\")\n        batch_definition = asset.add_batch_definition_whole_dataframe(name=\"whole_dataframe\")\n        return run_expectations(\n            context,\n            batch_definition=batch_definition,\n            checks=checks,\n            name=\"suite-uc\",\n            batch_parameters={\"dataframe\": df},\n        )\n\n\ndef build_unity_catalog_runner(\n    *, config: dict[str, Any], secret_ref: str | None, secret_store: SecretStore, catalog: str\n) -> UnityCatalogCheckRunner:\n    \"\"\"Build a runner from a UC `Connection`'s primitives + the target `catalog`.\n\n    Mirrors `build_snowflake_runner`: resolves the PAT eagerly and takes the raw\n    config dict (not the ORM model) to keep the adapter decoupled from `db/`.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not secret_ref:\n        raise ValueError(\"Unity Catalog connection requires secret_ref for the PAT\")\n    uc_config = UnityCatalogConfig.model_validate(config)\n    token = secret_store.get(secret_ref)\n    return UnityCatalogCheckRunner(config=uc_config, token=token, catalog=catalog)"

The batch\n# pattern is a regex whose **first capture group is the batch key**; `latest`\n# selects the greatest key, `specific` selects a named key. Resolution (filter +\n# select) is pure and fully tested; only the object listing is a live seam.\n\n\nclass BatchNotFoundError(ValueError):\n    \"\"\"No file matched the batch pattern (or the requested specific batch).\"\"\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass FileRef:\n    \"\"\"A listed object: its full key/blob path and last-modified time (if any).\"\"\"\n\n    path: str\n    last_modified: datetime | None = None\n\n\ndef resolve_batch(\n    files: list[FileRef], *, pattern: str, strategy: str = \"latest\", batch: str | None = None\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Pick one file's path from `files` per the batch `pattern` + `strategy`.\n\n    `pattern` is a regex `re.search`-ed against each path; its first capture group\n    (if any) is the batch key. `strategy`:\n\n    * ``latest`` — the greatest batch key (lexicographic — ISO dates sort right),\n      or, when the pattern has no capture group, the most recently modified file.\n    * ``specific`` — the file whose batch key equals `batch` (required).\n\n    Raises `BatchNotFoundError` (nothing matched / no such batch) or `ValueError`\n    (bad strategy, or `specific` without `batch`).\n    \"\"\"\n    compiled = re.compile(pattern)\n    matches = [(f, m) for f in files if (m := compiled.search(f.path))]\n    if not matches:\n        raise BatchNotFoundError(f\"no files matched batch pattern {pattern!r}\")\n\n    if strategy == \"specific\":\n        if batch is None:\n            raise ValueError(\"strategy 'specific' requires a batch key\")\n        hits = [f for f, m in matches if m.groups() and m.group(1) == batch]\n        if not hits:\n            raise BatchNotFoundError(f\"no file for batch {batch!r} under pattern {pattern!r}\")\n        return max(hits, key=lambda f: (f.last_modified or _MIN_DT, f.path)).path\n\n    if strategy != \"latest\":\n        raise ValueError(f\"unknown batch strategy {strategy!r}\")\n\n    keyed = [(f, m.group(1)) for f, m in matches if m.groups()]\n    if keyed:\n        return max(keyed, key=lambda fk: fk[1])[0].path\n    # No capture group → fall back to the storage modified time.\n    return max((f for f, _ in matches), key=lambda f: (f.last_modified or _MIN_DT, f.path)).path\n\n\ndef list_files(*, conn_type: str, config: dict[str, Any], prefix: str, secret: str) -> list[FileRef]:\n    \"\"\"List objects/blobs under `prefix` on a flat-file datasource (live seam).\"\"\"\n    if conn_type == \"s3\":\n        import boto3\n        from botocore.config import Config\n\n        cfg = S3Config.model_validate(config)\n        client = boto3.client(\n            \"s3\",\n            region_name=cfg.region,\n            aws_access_key_id=cfg.access_key_id,\n            aws_secret_access_key=secret,\n            config=Config(connect_timeout=_CONNECT_TIMEOUT, read_timeout=_READ_TIMEOUT),\n        )\n        paginator = client.get_paginator(\"list_objects_v2\")\n        refs: list[FileRef] = []\n        for page in paginator.paginate(Bucket=cfg.bucket, Prefix=prefix):\n            for obj in page.get(\"Contents\", []):\n                refs.append(FileRef(path=obj[\"Key\"], last_modified=obj.get(\"LastModified\")))\n        return refs\n\n    from azure.storage.blob import BlobServiceClient\n\n    acfg = AdlsConfig.model_validate(config)\n    client_az: Any = BlobServiceClient(account_url=acfg.account_url, credential=secret)\n    try:\n        container = client_az.get_container_client(acfg.container)\n        return [\n            FileRef(path=blob.name, last_modified=getattr(blob, \"last_modified\", None))\n            for blob in container.list_blobs(name_starts_with=prefix)\n        ]\n    finally:\n        client_az.close()\n\n\ndef resolve_batch_file(\n    *,\n    conn_type: str,\n    config: dict[str, Any],\n    secret: str,\n    prefix: str,\n    pattern: str,\n    strategy: str = \"latest\",\n    batch: str | None = None,\n) -> str:\n    \"\"\"List under `prefix`, then resolve the batch file path (list + `resolve_batch`).\"\"\"\n    files = list_files(conn_type=conn_type, config=config, prefix=prefix, secret=secret)\n    return resolve_batch(files, pattern=pattern, strategy=strategy, batch=batch)"

Batch resolution is built, tested, and on PR **#144** with CI running.

## Summary

`resolve_batch` resolves a batch regex (first capture group = batch key) to a single file — `latest` (max key, ISO-date-safe; mtime fallback when no group) or `specific`. The filter+select logic is pure and covered on every branch (8 tests); only the S3/ADLS listing is a live seam. It sits in `flatfile.py` next to the IO + runner, and `resolve_batch_file` composes list+resolve.

One thing I deliberately did **not** add: a ReDoS guard on the user regex. The pattern comes from trusted suite config (an authenticated editor authoring their own checks), so it's low-risk for v1 — but worth noting as a hardening item if check authoring ever opens up. I'll flag it if CI's CodeQL disagrees.

 from __future__ import annotations
 
 import io

+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from datetime import UTC, datetime
 from typing import Any
 
 import great_expectations as gx
@@ -36,6 +39,9 @@ _READ_TIMEOUT = 60
 
 _FILE_TYPES = {"adls_gen2", "s3"}
 
+# Sort floor for files the store reports without a modified time.
+_MIN_DT = datetime.min.replace(tzinfo=UTC)
+
 
 def format_from_path(path: str) -> str | None:
     """Infer the file format from the path extension (`None` if unrecognised)."""
@@ -146,3 +152,114 @@ def build_flatfile_runner(
         raise ValueError("flat-file connection requires secret_ref for the credential")
     secret = secret_store.get(secret_ref)
     return FlatFileCheckRunner(conn_type=conn_type, config=config, secret=secret)
+
+
+# ───────────────────────── batch resolution ────────────────────────
+#
+# Flat files usually arrive in batches — `orders_2026-06-01.csv`,
+# `orders_2026-06-02.csv`, … — and a check targets *one* batch. The batch
+# pattern is a regex whose **first capture group is the batch key**; `latest`
+# selects the greatest key, `specific` selects a named key. Resolution (filter +
+# select) is pure and fully tested; only the object listing is a live seam.
+
+
+class BatchNotFoundError(ValueError):
+    """No file matched the batch pattern (or the requested specific batch)."""
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class FileRef:
+    """A listed object: its full key/blob path and last-modified time (if any)."""
+
+    path: str
+    last_modified: datetime | None = None
+
+
+def resolve_batch(
+    files: list[FileRef], *, pattern: str, strategy: str = "latest", batch: str | None = None
+) -> str:
+    """Pick one file's path from `files` per the batch `pattern` + `strategy`.
+
+    `pattern` is a regex `re.search`-ed against each path; its first capture group
+    (if any) is the batch key. `strategy`:
+
+    * ``latest`` — the greatest batch key (lexicographic — ISO dates sort right),
+      or, when the pattern has no capture group, the most recently modified file.
+    * ``specific`` — the file whose batch key equals `batch` (required).
+
+    Raises `BatchNotFoundError` (nothing matched / no such batch) or `ValueError`
+    (bad strategy, or `specific` without `batch`).
+    """
+    compiled = re.compile(pattern)
+    matches = [(f, m) for f in files if (m := compiled.search(f.path))]
+    if not matches:
+        raise BatchNotFoundError(f"no files matched batch pattern {pattern!r}")
+
+    if strategy == "specific":
+        if batch is None:
+            raise ValueError("strategy 'specific' requires a batch key")
+        hits = [f for f, m in matches if m.groups() and m.group(1) == batch]
+        if not hits:
+            raise BatchNotFoundError(f"no file for batch {batch!r} under pattern {pattern!r}")
+        return max(hits, key=lambda f: (f.last_modified or _MIN_DT, f.path)).path
+
+    if strategy != "latest":
+        raise ValueError(f"unknown batch strategy {strategy!r}")
+
+    keyed = [(f, m.group(1)) for f, m in matches if m.groups()]
+    if keyed:
+        return max(keyed, key=lambda fk: fk[1])[0].path
+    # No capture group → fall back to the storage modified time.
+    return max((f for f, _ in matches), key=lambda f: (f.last_modified or _MIN_DT, f.path)).path
+
+
+def list_files(
+    *, conn_type: str, config: dict[str, Any], prefix: str, secret: str
+) -> list[FileRef]:
+    """List objects/blobs under `prefix` on a flat-file datasource (live seam)."""
+    if conn_type == "s3":
+        import boto3
+        from botocore.config import Config
+
+        cfg = S3Config.model_validate(config)
+        client = boto3.client(
+            "s3",
+            region_name=cfg.region,
+            aws_access_key_id=cfg.access_key_id,
+            aws_secret_access_key=secret,
+            config=Config(connect_timeout=_CONNECT_TIMEOUT, read_timeout=_READ_TIMEOUT),
+        )
+        paginator = client.get_paginator("list_objects_v2")
+        refs: list[FileRef] = []
+        for page in paginator.paginate(Bucket=cfg.bucket, Prefix=prefix):
+            for obj in page.get("Contents", []):
+                refs.append(FileRef(path=obj["Key"], last_modified=obj.get("LastModified")))
+        return refs
+
+    from azure.storage.blob import BlobServiceClient
+
+    acfg = AdlsConfig.model_validate(config)
+    client_az: Any = BlobServiceClient(account_url=acfg.account_url, credential=secret)
+    try:
+        container = client_az.get_container_client(acfg.container)
+        return [
+            FileRef(path=blob.name, last_modified=getattr(blob, "last_modified", None))
+            for blob in container.list_blobs(name_starts_with=prefix)
+        ]
+    finally:
+        client_az.close()
+
+
+def resolve_batch_file(
+    *,
+    conn_type: str,
+    config: dict[str, Any],
+    secret: str,
+    prefix: str,
+    pattern: str,
+    strategy: str = "latest",
+    batch: str | None = None,
+) -> str:
+    """List under `prefix`, then resolve the batch file path (list + `resolve_batch`)."""
+    files = list_files(conn_type=conn_type, config=config, prefix=prefix, secret=secret)
+    return resolve_batch(files, pattern=pattern, strategy=strategy, batch=batch)

Review complete. The diff is small and self-contained, so I did the angle analysis directly rather than fanning out 7 agents for ~115 lines. **Verified findings:**

1. **Correctness (real bug):** in `resolve_batch`'s `latest`/`keyed` branch, `m.group(1)` is `None` when the first capture group is *optional and doesn't participate* (e.g. `orders_(\d+)?\.csv` on `orders_.csv`). `m.groups()` is still truthy `(None,)`, so it enters `keyed`, and `max(..., key=lambda fk: fk[1])` then compares `None` against a `str` → **TypeError**.
2. **Correctness (minor):** an invalid `pattern` makes `re.compile` raise `re.error`, which is **not** a `ValueError`/`BatchNotFoundError` — contradicting the docstring; a future API caller would get a 500 instead of a clean 422.
3. **Cleanup (DRY):** the S3 `boto3.client(...)` and ADLS `BlobServiceClient(...)` construction is duplicated verbatim between `download_bytes` and `list_files`.

Let me post these to the PR, then fix #1 and #2 (correctness) plus #3 (extraction):

After full cross-file tracing, the only material integration finding is the worker not dispatching the new runners (finding 1); finding 2 is a contract/usability gap specific to UC; finding 3 confirms the dispatch is actually closed (no silent wrong-branch). Items 1, 2 (catalog resolution), and 4 (GX name collision) traced clean:

- **Item 1 (Snowflake path):** `build_connection_string` is reused byte-for-byte; `_engine_args` only *adds* login/network timeouts in `connect_args` for the new profiler path. No regression to the existing Snowflake CheckRunner.
- **Item 2 (catalog consistency):** Verified against `databricks-sql-connector==3.7.0`'s dialect source. `create_connect_args` reads `catalog` from the URL query into `self.catalog`; `get_columns` reflects with `catalog_name=self.catalog, schema_name=schema`. So the runner's URL-pinned-catalog + `read_sql_table(table, schema=schema)` resolves to `catalog.schema.table` — identical to the profiler's explicit 3-part `quoted_name(f"{catalog}.{schema}", quote=False)` qualification (confirmed it renders `cat.sch.tbl`). The two paths are consistent.
- **Item 4 (GX name collision):** Each `run_checks`/`profile` creates its own ephemeral `gx.get_context`, registering exactly one `suite-{name}` + one `vd-{name}`. No within-context collision; contexts are per-call. Clean.
- **Item 5 (protocol):** UC needs `catalog`, which is correctly bound at construction (`build_unity_catalog_runner`) rather than in the protocol's `run_checks`, so the protocol stays uniform. `dryrun_service` gates to `{"snowflake"}` (422 otherwise). The only polymorphic break is the worker (finding 1).

def profile_file(
    connection: Connection,
    *,
    path: str,
    file_format: str | None,
    columns: list[str],
    top_n: int,
    secret_store: SecretStore,
) -> ProfileResult:
    """Profile `columns` of a flat file on `connection` (ADLS Gen2 / S3).

    Raises `ProfileTargetInvalidError` (422) for an unknown format,
    `ProfileColumnNotFoundError` (422) for a missing column, and
    `ProfileFailedError` (502) if the file can't be read — the underlying
    exception is never echoed (it can carry credential/endpoint fragments).
    """
    fmt = infer_file_format(path, file_format)
    try:
        df = _read_dataframe(
            connection, path=path, file_format=fmt, columns=columns, secret_store=secret_store
        )
    except Exception as exc:
        log.warning(
            "column_profile_failed", connection_type=connection.type, error_type=type(exc).__name__
        )
        raise ProfileFailedError(
            "column profile could not read the file", detail={"path": path}
        ) from exc

    return profile_dataframe(df, columns=columns, top_n=top_n, path=path, file_format=fmt)

) -> ProfileResult:
    """Build the `ProfileResult` from raw query rows (pure, warehouse-free)."""
    row_count = int(aggregate["row_count"])
    profiles: list[ColumnProfile] = []
    for i, col in enumerate(columns):
        nulls = int(aggregate[f"nulls_{i}"])

Not a live break (run path is Week-5-gated), but the thing to fix when wiring Week-5 runner dispatch.

**Verified but *not* filed** (so you know they were checked, not missed):
- The `gx_runner` extraction is behavior-preserving — `run_expectations(batch_parameters=None)` is equivalent to the old bare `run()` (GX guards `if batch_parameters:`); all snowflake re-exports resolve; no tests weakened (103 passed).
- UC catalog resolution is consistent — URL-pinned catalog + `read_sql_table(schema=…)` resolves to `catalog.schema.table`, matching the profiler's 3-part `quoted_name` (checked against the databricks dialect source).

- pandas `NA` from pyarrow `min()` is guarded by `dropna()` + the `len(non_null)` check.

**Minor drift I'll just flag (no issue unless you want one):** the S3 read timeout drifted 30s→60s during the extraction; `_SUPPORTED_FORMATS` duplicates `format_from_path`'s extension knowledge; and the SQL profiler does N+1 warehouse round-trips (fine for a ≤50-column authoring aid, but it scales linearly).

More lenient than before; a hung S3 read now ties up a worker thread twice as long. Confirm 60s is intentional (full-file reads may legitimately need longer than a profiler sample) vs accidental drift, and align the two constants.\n\n### 2. `_SUPPORTED_FORMATS` duplicates `format_from_path`\n[`infer_file_format`](backend/app/services/profile_service.py#L333) calls `flatfile.format_from_path(path)` then checks membership in [`_SUPPORTED_FORMATS = {\"csv\",\"parquet\"}`](backend/app/services/profile_service.py#L62). But `format_from_path` already only ever returns `csv`/`parquet`/`None`, so the supported-format set is expressed twice. Add JSON to `format_from_path` and the profiler silently still rejects it. Derive the supported set from `format_from_path`, or drop the redundant check.\n\n### 3. Duplicated stat contract: SQL vs pandas\nThe per-column statistic definitions (null_fraction = nulls/row_count with the row_count==0 guard, distinct excludes nulls, top_values = non-null desc by count) are implemented twice with no shared code — once in SQL via [`assemble_profile`](backend/app/services/profile_service.py#L195) and once in pandas via [`profile_dataframe`](backend/app/services/profile_service.py#L362). A definitional change must be made in both or the two datasource families disagree for the same logical data. (Hard to fully DRY across SQL vs pandas, but the *contract* could be captured in one place / a shared test.)\n\n### 4. N+1 warehouse round-trips in the SQL profiler\n[`profile_table`](backend/app/services/profile_service.py#L304) issues 1 aggregate query + one top-values query **per column** in a Python loop. For a 50-column profile that's 51 sequential warehouse queries; against a cold SQL warehouse (~1s/query) that's ~50s of wall time for an interactive authoring aid. Acceptable for v1 (≤50-col cap), but consider batching the top-values queries (UNION ALL / a single windowed query) if profiler latency becomes a problem.\n\n### 5. Parquet footer read twice (minor)\n[`_read_dataframe`](backend/app/services/profile_service.py#L440) reads `pq.ParquetFile(raw).schema.names` to filter requested columns to those present, then re-parses with `pd.read_parquet(columns=present)`. The footer read is cheap, and it's needed so `read_parquet` doesn't raise on an absent column — but the column-presence logic now lives in two places (the pre-read filter and `profile_dataframe`'s missing-column 422 check). --- current profile_dataframe ---
def profile_dataframe(
    df: Any, *, columns: list[str], top_n: int, path: str, file_format: str
) -> ProfileResult:
    """Compute per-column stats from an in-memory dataframe (pure, no I/O).

    Raises `ProfileColumnNotFoundError` (422) if a requested column isn't in the
    frame — a clean error instead of a KeyError 500.
    """
    missing = [c for c in columns if c not in df.columns]
    if missing:
        raise ProfileColumnNotFoundError(
            "requested column(s) not in the file",
            detail={"missing": missing, "available": [str(c) for c in df.columns][:50]},
        )
    row_count = len(df)
    profiles: list[ColumnProfile] = []
    for col in columns:
        series = df[col]
        null_count = int(series.isna().sum())
        non_null = series.dropna()
        counts = non_null.value_counts().head(top_n)
        profiles.append(
            ColumnProfile(
                column=col,
                null_count=null_count,
                null_fraction=(null_count / row_count) if row_count else 0.0,
                distinct_count=int(non_null.nunique()),
                min_value=sanitize_json(_to_native(non_null.min())) if len(non_null) else None,
                max_value=sanitize_json(_to_native(non_null.max())) if len(non_null) else None,
                top_values=[
                    {"value": sanitize_json(_to_native(value)), "count": int(count)}
                    for value, count in counts.items()
                ],
            )
        )
    return ProfileResult(path=path, file_format=file_format, row_count=row_count, columns=profiles)


def _read_dataframe(
    connection: Connection,
    *,
    path: str,
    file_format: str,
    columns: list[str],
    secret_store: SecretStore,

def _typed_connection(db_session: Any, ctype: str, config: dict[str, Any]) -> Connection:
    owner = User(aad_object_id=uuid.uuid4().hex, email=f"{ctype}@ex")
    db_session.add(owner)
    db_session.flush()
    conn = Connection(
        name=f"{ctype}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}",
        type=ctype,
        env="dev",
        config=config,
        created_by=owner.id,
    )
    db_session.add(conn)
    db_session.commit()
    return conn
```

# ── profile_dataframe robustness (messy columns must not raise) ──

import pandas as pd  # noqa: E402

from backend.app.services.profile_service import profile_dataframe  # noqa: E402


def test_profile_dataframe_mixed_type_column_nulls_minmax_not_raise() -> None:
    df = pd.DataFrame({"amount": [10, "N/A", 20, "N/A"]})  # uncomparable object column
    col = profile_dataframe(
        df, columns=["amount"], top_n=5, path="x.csv", file_format="csv"
    ).columns[0]
    assert col.min_value is None and col.max_value is None  # min/max can't compare → null
    assert col.distinct_count == 3  # hashable → computed
    assert col.top_values[0] == {"value": "N/A", "count": 2}
    assert col.null_count == 0


def test_profile_dataframe_unhashable_column_nulls_distinct() -> None:
    df = pd.DataFrame({"tags": [[1], [2], [1]]})  # unhashable cells
    col = profile_dataframe(df, columns=["tags"], top_n=5, path="x.csv", file_format="csv").columns[
        0
    ]
    assert col.distinct_count is None  # nunique can't hash → null, no crash
    assert col.null_count == 0

+def _profile_series(column: str, series: Any, *, row_count: int, top_n: int) -> ColumnProfile:
+    """Per-column stats, degrading a messy column to nulls instead of 500-ing.
+
+    `null_count` is always computable, but a real-world flat file can hold a
+    column the stats can't process: min/max raise on **uncomparable** mixed types
+    (e.g. ints and strings in one object column), and distinct/value_counts raise
+    on **unhashable** cells (nested list/dict values from Parquet). Each of those
+    is guarded independently so one bad column yields null stats for itself rather
+    than failing the whole profile request.
+    """
+    null_count = int(series.isna().sum())
+    non_null = series.dropna()
+    try:
+        minimum = _to_native(non_null.min()) if len(non_null) else None
+        maximum = _to_native(non_null.max()) if len(non_null) else None
+    except (TypeError, ValueError):
+        minimum = maximum = None
+    try:
+        distinct: int | None = int(non_null.nunique())
+    except (TypeError, ValueError):
+        distinct = None
+    try:
+        counts = non_null.value_counts().head(top_n)
+        top = [
+            {"value": sanitize_json(_to_native(value)), "count": int(count)}
+            for value, count in counts.items()
+        ]
+    except (TypeError, ValueError):
+        top = []
+    return ColumnProfile(
+        column=column,
+        null_count=null_count,
+        null_fraction=(null_count / row_count) if row_count else 0.0,
+        distinct_count=distinct,
+        min_value=sanitize_json(minimum),
+        max_value=sanitize_json(maximum),
+        top_values=top,
+    )
+

> DEVELOPER

Why our unit tests are not able to catch these bugs? are we not covering the full scope? or are we missing adding them after new changes are added?

> AGENT

Good question — and the honest answer is that it's mostly a **test-design** gap, not a discipline gap. We *did* add tests with each change (the profiler sat at ~94% line coverage when these merged), and the scope wasn't really "uncovered." The problem is more specific and more interesting. Three distinct mechanisms, each tied to one of the bugs:

## 1. Happy-path / clean-input bias (the 500 bug)
Our `profile_dataframe` tests fed *well-behaved* data — `[10, 20, 20]`, `["x", "y"]`, plus a few edges we *did* think of (empty, all-null, NaN). Every line ran, so coverage looked great. But the bug lived in input territory we never fed: a column whose values can't be **compared** (`min()` on mixed int/str) or **hashed** (`nunique()` on lists).

The key insight: **line coverage measures lines, not input space.** The original code had no `try/except` — it just *assumed* clean data. There was no uncovered line for the coverage tool to flag; the missing case was an unstated assumption, which coverage is blind to. 94% covered, 0% adversarial.

## 2. Mocking hid the very seam under test (the 502 bug)
The missing-credential check lived *inside* `_open_connection` / `_read_dataframe` — and every profiler endpoint test **mocks those functions**. So the credential path (and its error mapping) was never actually executed in a test. The test connections even had `secret_ref=None`, but it never mattered because the code that checks it was stubbed out. Classic: we mocked away the thing we needed to validate, and never wrote the negative-path test.

## 3. The test shared the fix's blind spot (the pyarrow gap)
My own fix's "unhashable" test used a numpy object column (`[[1],[2]]`) → `TypeError` (caught). I didn't test the **pyarrow-backed Parquet** variant → `ArrowNotImplementedError` (not caught). Tests written by the same person, at the same time, with the same mental model as the code **inherit its blind spots**. That's *why review caught it and the test didn't* — review is an independent lens; a self-authored test is not.

## So which of your two framings is it?
Neither cleanly. We added tests after changes (discipline was fine) and coverage was decent (scope wasn't the issue). What we're short on is **failure-mode and adversarial-input tests** for code that eats arbitrary external data — a profiler ingesting user files is exactly where "what if the data is garbage?" matters most, and that's the category we under-test.

## Concrete, cheap things that would close the gap

| Lever | Catches |
|---|---|
| **Adversarial-input fixtures** for any data-ingesting function (mixed types, unhashable, empty, all-null, huge, unicode, both numpy & pyarrow backends) | the 500 bug, the pyarrow gap |
| **Don't mock the seam you're validating** — at least one test that exercises the real credential/error path | the 502 bug |
| **Branch coverage** (not just line) + **mutation testing** | mutation testing would have flagged `except (TypeError, ValueError)` directly — flip it and tests still pass, proving the exception type was unpinned. It's the one tool that specifically finds "covered but not asserted." |
| **Review writes/scrutinizes the negative-path tests** | author blind spots |

The deeper point: tests and review catch *different* bug classes — tests catch regressions on known inputs; review catches unhandled-input *reasoning*. The system worked (review caught what tests missed), but we can tilt the tests to catch more.

Want me to act on any of these? Concretely, I'd suggest: (a) add a small shared adversarial-input test helper and apply it to the profiler + the runners, and/or (b) spike `mutmut`/`cosmic-ray` mutation testing on `profile_service` to see what else is "covered but unasserted." I can also save this as a testing working-agreement so it's applied going forward. Your call on scope.

This module centralises that\nhostile-input set so any function that processes a DataFrame can be swept with\nthe same battery, and asserts the one contract that matters at the edge: the\noutput is **plain JSON** (no NaN/Inf, no exotic scalars) and never raised.\n\n`ADVERSARIAL_FRAMES` is `(id, DataFrame)` pairs, each a single column named\n``x``. Pass it to `pytest.mark.parametrize`. `assert_json_safe(value)` enforces\nthe JSON contract on any emitted scalar/structure.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport io\nimport json\nfrom typing import Any\n\nimport pandas as pd\n\n\ndef _parquet_roundtrip(frame: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:\n    \"\"\"Round-trip through Parquet with the Arrow backend the profiler/runner use.\n\n    Arrow-backed columns raise *different* exception types than numpy ones (e.g.\n    ``ArrowNotImplementedError`` vs ``TypeError``), so the Arrow variants are the\n    ones that catch over-narrow ``except`` clauses.\n    \"\"\"\n    buf = io.BytesIO()\n    frame.to_parquet(buf)\n    buf.seek(0)\n    return pd.read_parquet(buf, dtype_backend=\"pyarrow\")\n\n\nADVERSARIAL_FRAMES: list[tuple[str, pd.DataFrame]] = [\n    # — object columns the numpy way —\n    (\"mixed_int_str\", pd.DataFrame({\"x\": [10, \"N/A\", 20, \"N/A\"]})),\n    (\"mixed_with_none\", pd.DataFrame({\"x\": [1, None, \"x\", 2.5]})),\n    (\"all_null\", pd.DataFrame({\"x\": [None, None, None]})),\n    (\"empty_rows\", pd.DataFrame({\"x\": pd.Series([], dtype=\"object\")})),\n    (\"unhashable_list_numpy\", pd.DataFrame({\"x\": [[1], [2], [1]]})),\n    (\"unhashable_dict\", pd.DataFrame({\"x\": [{\"a\": 1}, {\"b\": 2}]})),\n    # the runner must map a real GX run over hostile data to a SuiteOutcome, not crash.\n    monkeypatch.setattr(flatfile, \"read_dataframe\", lambda **k: frame)\n    runner = flatfile.FlatFileCheckRunner(conn_type=\"s3\", config={}, secret=\"x\")\n    outcome = runner.run_checks(\n        table=\"f.parquet\",\n        schema=None,\n        checks=[CheckSpec(\"expect_table_row_count_to_be_between\", {\"min_value\": 0, \"max_value\": 10**9})],\n    )\n    assert isinstance(outcome.success, bool)\n    assert outcome.checks[0].expectation_type == \"expect_table_row_count_to_be_between\"\nPYEOF\nconda run -n dataq black backend/tests/services/test_profile_service.py backend/tests/datasources/test_flatfile.py backend/tests/support/adversarial.py >/dev/null 2>&1\nconda run -n dataq ruff check backend/tests/support/ backend/tests/services/test_profile_service.py backend/tests/datasources/test_flatfile.py 2>&1 | tail -3",

High line coverage is not enough — the column profiler sat at ~94% line coverage and still 500'd on a mixed-type column, because *line coverage measures lines, not input space* (issues #145/#147).\n\n**Why:** the bugs review kept catching (profiler 500 on uncomparable/unhashable columns, pyarrow `ArrowNotImplementedError` slipping past a narrow `except`, 502-instead-of-422 for a missing credential) were all \"covered\" code running with inputs the tests never fed. Tests written alongside the code share its blind spots, so they confirm the cases the author imagined — not the ones they didn't.\n\n**How to apply:**\n- **Adversarial inputs for any data-ingesting function** (file, DataFrame, user query). Sweep it with the shared battery in `backend/tests/support/adversarial.py` (`ADVERSARIAL_FRAMES` + `assert_json_safe`): mixed types, unhashable cells, NaN/Inf, bytes, empty, **and both numpy & pyarrow backends** (they raise different exception types — the pyarrow variant is what catches over-narrow `except` clauses). Contract: never raise, emit plain JSON.\n- **Don't mock the seam you're validating.** If the behaviour under test lives inside a stubbed function, the test proves nothing about it. Pushed. Let me answer your question fully while CI runs:

**No — not `requirements.txt`, and deliberately not `requirements-dev.txt` either.** Here's the layering reasoning:

- `requirements.txt` = **runtime hub** (ships in the container). mutmut is a test tool → never here.
- `requirements-dev.txt` = what **CI installs** *and* what **`pip-audit` gates merges on** (per CLAUDE.md). mutmut never runs in CI, and it pulls `pony`/`parso`/etc. — adding it would bloat every CI job and put those transitive deps on the CVE merge-gate for zero benefit.
- So I added **`backend/requirements-mutation.txt`** — pinned (`mutmut==2.5.0`) and one-command installable (`pip install -r`), but *not* `-r`'d by anything, so it's inert to CI. That gives you the reproducibility you were after without the CI/audit cost.

"""Tests for the run/result persistence service.

No database or GX: a fake Session records what would be persisted, model
instances are built in memory with explicit ids, and a fake CheckRunner returns
canned outcomes (or raises). This keeps the service's lifecycle + mapping logic
under test independent of Postgres and Snowflake.
"""

import uuid
from decimal import Decimal

from backend.app.datasources.base import CheckOutcome, CheckSpec, SuiteOutcome
from backend.app.db.models import Check, Result, Run
from backend.app.services import run_service


class FakeSession:
    """Records add_all'd rows; counts commits/rollbacks. `add_all_raises` simulates
    a persistence failure (e.g. DB error) after the adapter has already run."""

    def __init__(self, *, add_all_raises: Exception | None = None) -> None:
        self.added: list[Result] = []
        self.commits = 0
        self.rollbacks = 0
        self._add_all_raises = add_all_raises

    def add_all(self, rows: list[Result]) -> None:
        if self._add_all_raises is not None:
            raise self._add_all_raises
        self.added.extend(rows)

    def commit(self) -> None:
        self.commits += 1

    def rollback(self) -> None:
        self.rollbacks += 1


class FakeRunner:
    def __init__(
        self, outcome: SuiteOutcome | None = None, raises: Exception | None = None
    ) -> None:
        self._outcome = outcome
        self._raises = raises
        self.called_with: dict[str, object] | None = None

    def run_checks(
        self, *, table: str, schema: str | None, checks: list[CheckSpec]
    ) -> SuiteOutcome:
        self.called_with = {"table": table, "schema": schema, "checks": checks}
        if self._raises is not None:
            raise self._raises
        assert self._outcome is not None
        return self._outcome


def _run() -> Run:
    return Run(id=uuid.uuid4(), suite_id=uuid.uuid4(), status="queued")

+            expectation_type=c["type"],
+            config=c["config"],
+        )
+        for c in _CHECKS
+    ]
+    db_session.add_all(checks)
+    db_session.flush()
+    return suite, checks
+
+
+def _queued_run(db_session: Any, suite: Suite) -> Run:
+    run = Run(suite_id=suite.id, status="queued")
+    db_session.add(run)
+    db_session.commit()
+    return run

### 5. docs/architecture.md

**Finding 5.1 — "GX execution is Celery-only" invariant is violated by the dry-run endpoint (RED flag — documentation inconsistency with shipped code)**
`docs/architecture.md` line 79:
```
**GX execution is Celery-only.** FastAPI never calls GX directly; it enqueues tasks.
```
`backend/app/services/dryrun_service.py` calls `build_snowflake_runner(...)` and invokes GX synchronously in a FastAPI threadpool (`run_in_threadpool` via FastAPI's `BackgroundTasks` equivalent). The `dryrun_service` docstring itself states: `Synchronous + blocking (Snowflake connect + GX): the API runs it in a threadpool.` This is a deliberate, intentional exception for the preview use case (single check, no persistence, not a scheduled run), but the architecture.md invariant does not acknowledge it.

This is not a merge-blocker (the code is already shipped), but the invariant in the architecture documentation is now factually wrong as a blanket statement. Suggest updating to: `GX execution for suite runs is Celery-only. FastAPI never enqueues a full suite run directly. Exception: the check dry-run endpoint (POST /suites/{id}/checks/dryrun) runs a single GX check synchronously in a threadpool for preview purposes and persists nothing.`

**Finding 5.2 — Diagram does not show FastAPI → datasource path for profiler/dry-run (YELLOW)**
The Mermaid diagram shows only `Celery → GX checks → Snowflake / ADLS / UC`. Now that `POST /suites/{id}/profile` (profiler, SQL + pandas) and `POST /suites/{id}/checks/dryrun` (GX via threadpool) both originate directly from FastAPI, there is an undocumented FastAPI → datasource path. The diagram's `Celery` node is the only path shown to datasources.

The diagram need not capture every endpoint, but the omission reinforces the now-incorrect "Celery-only" invariant. If the invariant is updated (Finding 5.1), adding a dashed `FastAPI --read-only/preview--> datasources` edge (or a note) would make the diagram consistent.

**Finding 5.3 — Diagram and narrative accurately describe the 4 datasources and orchestration split (PASS)**
`SF`, `ADLS`, `UC` nodes are present. `Orch` node correctly represents ADF + Airflow as orchestration (not datasources). The `Monitor` and `Teams` nodes are correct. `CheckRunner`, `gx_runner`, and profiler are implementation details below the diagram's level of abstraction and do not need to appear.

This glob claim is correct in spirit but rule 17 doesn't distinguish `requirements-mutation.txt` as isolated from CI. Rule 4a in §A correctly calls this out, but a reader of §C rule 17 has no pointer to the mutation exception. This is minor — the two rules are in the same document — but cross-referencing would clarify: "(`requirements-mutation.txt` is excluded from CI; see rule 4a)".

**Finding 6.3 — Rule 21 typecheck description ("the single source of truth — CI's mypy + pytest jobs install from it") is imprecise (YELLOW)**
`CONTRIBUTING.md` line 72 calls `requirements-typecheck.txt` "the single source of truth" for mypy. In practice `requirements-tooling.txt` is what installs mypy itself (and Black/Ruff/Bandit/pre-commit), while `requirements-typecheck.txt` installs the typed stubs and typed third-party packages mypy needs to typecheck the application code. Both are `-r`'d by `requirements-dev.txt`. The phrase "single source of truth" for `requirements-typecheck.txt` is not wrong if interpreted narrowly as "where the typed stubs live", but it is potentially confusing now that `requirements-tooling.txt` also exists and affects the mypy install. No immediate action required, but the description could be made more precise.
